data.description:
# Contention-queue sweep: collapse depth/wait once reservations land

## Problem statement

The contention queue converts wait time into a chance of staying local. On the
current 60 s budget the conversion has already failed: in the 3.3 h after the
120 s → 60 s change went live, 180 local queue events produced **38 wins and
142 losses, every loss at the full 60 s** — 8 705 s (≈2.4 h) of dead wait that
ended on a remote provider anyway. The two remaining knobs
(`contention_queue_max_wait_seconds: 60`, `contention_queue_max_depth: 8`) are
load-shedding knobs, and neither separates a slow-but-winnable wait from a
hopeless one.

Once cooperating clients reserve capacity (`POST /llama/local/reserve`,
`LP-0MVIKPCSG002B0NL`, live since 2026-10-21), the queue no longer needs to be
the primary waiting mechanism: it only has to be a small safety net for
stragglers and non-cooperating clients.

## Users

- As an **operator**, I want the fallback queue to be a bounded straggler net,
  not a 60 s parking lot, so dead local wait stops competing with real local
  work.
- As a **cooperating client** (herdr dispatcher), I want my only waits to be
  ticket-backed reserved waits, so I can plan around a wait I hold rather than
  an invisible proxy-side park.
- As a **non-cooperating client**, I still want a short grace window before the
  proxy detours to a remote provider, so a slot that frees within seconds is
  still usable.

## Evidence appendix (measurements)

**Current 60 s era** — `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log*`, 2026-10-22 19:00 →
22:18 (3.3 h, the window since the proxy restarted on the 60 s config):

| metric | value |
|---|---|
| queue events (`contention_queue_dispatch` + `contention_queue_fallback_after_queue`) | 180 |
| wins | 38 (21 %) |
| losses | 142 (79 %) — **all** at full budget (`queued_duration≈60.0s`) |
| aggregate dead wait | 8 705 s (≈2.4 h) |
| win wait p50 / p75 / p90 / max | 39.5 s / 48.1 s / 59.8 s / 112.9 s |
| loss reason split | 95 `local_lease_active`, 47 none |

Retained wins by candidate budget (same window): 10 s → 6/38 (16 %),
15 s → 6/38 (16 %), **20 s → 9/38 (24 %)**, **30 s → 13/38 (34 %)**,
45 s → 23/38 (60 %), 60 s → 35/38 (92 %).

**Prior 120 s era** (for continuity, from the creating comment): 2026-10-21
14:56 → 17:00, 372 queue events — 43 wins (median wait 65 s) versus 329 losses,
283 (86 %) of which would have needed ≥120 s under any cap; 261 requests
queued and then went remote, 215 after the full budget (25 804 s aggregate
wait); queue depth reached 7 in-window.

**Reservation adoption** — server endpoint shipped (`LP-0MVIKPCSG002B0NL`,
`completed`), status payload exposes `reserved_issued/used/cancelled/expired`,
and the dispatch path logs `local_admission_reserve_claimed`. Observed usage in
the last 24 h of `proxy.log*`: **0** claimed tickets, `reserved_issued: 0`. The
client-side item `WL-0MVIKRFP0005JDL8` is still `open`/`idea`, so no client
sends `X-Local-Reservation` / `X-Local-Preference` yet.

**Guard activity in the same 3.3 h window**: 870 refusals — 376 on the queue
path (`reason=eta_exceeds_budget`) and 494 on the direct free-slot path
(`reason=eta_exceeds_budget_direct`). The ETA guard is already doing the bulk
of the shedding; the *residual* losses that still park for the full budget sit
mostly on the lease-retention branch (`reason=local_lease_active`, 95 of 142).

## Desired change (the sweep)

1. **Target values** — `proxy/config.yaml`:

   ```yaml
   contention_queue_max_wait_seconds: 30   # was 60 (was 120 in LP-0MVIQ0EXV00673HO)
   contention_queue_max_depth: 2           # was 8
   ```

   30 s retains a third of current wins while capping dead wait at 30 s; depth
   2 keeps a straggler net without the observed 7-deep parking lot. Both values
   stay inside the existing clamps (`wait` ∈ [1, guardrail], `depth` ∈ [1, 16]).

2. **Trigger (decoupled from client adoption — operator decision 2026-10-22)**
   — the sweep is *not* gated on `WL-0MVIKRFP0005JDL8`. Preconditions: the
   reservation endpoint is live (met 2026-10-21) **and** a ≥24 h pre-flip
   baseline exists at 60 s/depth 8 (≈55 queue events/h → ~1 300 events/day;
   the 3.3 h intake window is the seed, extend before flipping).
   Post-flip observation: 7 days / ≥1 000 queue events.

3. **Flip criteria** (measured over the observation window against the 24 h
   pre-flip baseline) — keep the sweep if **all** hold:
   - aggregate dead wait per hour falls by ≥50 %;
   - residual queue wins stay ≥20 % of queue events (i.e. the net still
     converts something);
   - remote dispatch volume rises by <20 % relative (no flood of paid
     fallbacks).

4. **Rollback** — revert the two values to 60 / 8, restart the proxy (config
   change requires a restart), and record the observed metrics in this item.
   `contention_queue_lease_grace_seconds: 300` and
   `contention_queue_policy: queue` are unchanged; the lease grace stays above
   the new budget so a returning session still re-queues as retained.

5. **Residual-queue telemetry (reporting, not a gate)** — a windowed report
   counting (a) ticket-backed dispatches (`local_admission_reserve_claimed`),
   (b) residual queue wins at or below the sweep budget
   (`contention_queue_dispatch … queued_duration=`), (c) residual queue losses
   and their aggregate wait (`contention_queue_fallback_after_queue …
   queued_duration=`), split by `reason` so lease-active losses are visible
   separately (95/142 today). Source: the log lines, **not** new status
   counters — cumulative counters were deliberately removed in
   `LP-0MU4NACW9001WKBP` and log parsing is the established consumer pattern.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **AC1 — sweep plan.** This item records the target values (30 s / depth 2),
   the trigger (endpoint live + ≥24 h 60 s baseline, decoupled from client
   adoption per operator decision 2026-10-22), the 7-day observation window,
   the flip criteria above, and the two-line rollback with proxy restart;
   each value justified by the win/loss distributions in the evidence
   appendix.
2. **AC2 — single-source budget.** The shortened budget reaches the admission
   guard's `wait_budget_seconds` and `POST /llama/local/reserve`'s budget
   through the **same** resolver (`prefill_eta.wait_budget_seconds`) — no
   second constant, no per-call default — with tests asserting that
   `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds: 30` is what both the guard and the
   reservation endpoint compare against, and that `depth: 2` is accepted and
   clamped only outside [1, 16].
3. **AC3 — residual-queue telemetry.** A windowed report (script + test) emits
   (a) ticket-backed dispatch count, (b) residual queue wins at or below the
   sweep budget, (c) residual queue losses with aggregate wait and a `reason`
   split (lease-active vs other) for a stated window; the report is run and its
   numbers recorded on this item when the sweep is evaluated. Ticket counts are
   reported, not used as a flip gate. Data comes from the existing log events
   (reusing `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/log_parser.py` as a library
   where practical); **no new status counters** — `LP-0MU4NACW9001WKBP` removed
   the cumulative ones on purpose.
4. **AC4 — tests / validation.** Unit tests cover the swept values end to end:
   config validation accepts 30/2, the queue resolver returns 30 s, a waiter
   beyond depth 2 falls back immediately instead of enqueueing, and a waiter
   that exceeds 30 s falls back at 30 s; fixtures/tests that assume the
   60 s / 8 defaults are updated rather than left stale.
5. **AC5 — docs.** `proxy/config.yaml` comments and `proxy/docs/routing.md`
   describe the queue as a straggler safety net for non-cooperating clients,
   with reservations as the primary cooperative path, and record the
   60 → 30 s / 8 → 2 change with its measurement dates, flip criteria and
   rollback.
6. **AC6 — documentation & suite.** All related documentation is updated to
   reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki
   or docs site entries; full project test suite must pass with the new
   changes.

## Constraints

- Fail-open semantics of the admission guard are unchanged (uncalibrated →
  admit).
- One budget, one resolver: no new knob, no per-reason budget (operator
  decision 2026-10-22); the lease-active split is a *reporting* dimension
  only.
- Out of scope: queue removal (a zero-wait proxy has no local concurrency
  tolerance at all), slot count, ctx-size, the ETA guard's model, and client
  reservation adoption (`WL-0MVIKRFP0005JDL8`).
- Changing either value requires a proxy restart; the sweep must be applied in
  a quiet window and announced in the item comment trail.

## Existing state

- `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds: 60`, `contention_queue_max_depth: 8`,
  `contention_queue_policy: queue`, `contention_queue_lease_grace_seconds: 300`
  (`proxy/config.yaml` ~1651–1683).
- `_get_contention_queue_config()` clamps wait to
  [1, `session_guardrail_max_runtime_seconds`] and depth to [1, 16], logging
  and coercing invalid values.
- `prefill_eta.wait_budget_seconds(config, priority)` is the single resolver
  used by the guard, `/reserve` and `provider.py`.
- Queue telemetry exists as log events only (`contention_queue_dispatch`,
  `contention_queue_fallback_after_queue`); reservation counters exist as
  process-lifetime counters in `/llama/local/status`, so a *windowed* report
  must come from the logs.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/config.yaml` — sweep the two values, rewrite the surrounding comment
  block (line ~1651) with the new evidence and the rollback note.
- `proxy/proxy/prefill_eta.py` — `wait_budget_seconds()`; assert the single
  resolver path (no change expected beyond a comment).
- `proxy/proxy/router.py` — `_get_contention_queue_config()` clamps; confirm
  30/2 pass through unchanged.
- `proxy/proxy/admission_reserve.py` — budget sourced from the resolver
  (comment / assertion only if it hard-codes anything).
- `proxy/proxy/contention_queue.py` — `wait_for_local_slot()` depth-cap
  behaviour (immediate fallback beyond depth).
- `proxy/proxy/handlers.py` — status payload (`contention_queue_depth`, live
  depth and reservation counters); no new cumulative counters are added here
  (see `LP-0MU4NACW9001WKBP`).
- `proxy/tests/test_contention_queue.py`, `proxy/tests/test_local_admission_guard.py`,
  `proxy/tests/test_admission_reserve.py`,
  `proxy/tests/test_llama_local_status.py` — updates for the swept defaults.
- `proxy/docs/routing.md` — queue/reservation description and the recorded
  change (lines ~674, 731, 897–899).
- `scripts/contention_queue_sweep_report.py` (new) — windowed residual-queue
  report for AC3; parses `proxy.log*` and may import
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/log_parser.py` as a library (read-only
  use; that skill's files are not edited here). Modelled on
  `scripts/idle_admit_impact.py`. Extending the daily proxy usage report with the
  same breakdown is a possible follow-up, not part of this item.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Lost local wins become remote spend.** 30 s converts ~29 of the current 38
  wins per 3.3 h into remote dispatches; the flip criteria cap that at +20 %
  remote volume and the rollback is two lines. *Assumption (operator,
  2026-10-22):* the dead-wait saving is worth the trade even before clients
  reserve.
- **Reservations unused today.** No client sends `X-Local-Reservation` yet, so
  the "queue is only for stragglers" premise is aspirational until
  `WL-0MVIKRFP0005JDL8` lands; the sweep is justified on queue economics
  instead, and AC3 keeps ticket counts visible so the premise can be re-checked
  when adoption arrives.
- **Lease-active losses dominate the residual (95/142).** A 30 s budget shortens
  the wait for returning lease owners too. Reported separately (AC3); a
  per-reason budget is explicitly out of scope (would be a second mechanism
  needing its own evidence).
- **Guard interaction.** The ETA guard fires before queueing; a shorter budget
  makes it stricter (fewer queued waits, more direct fallbacks), so the
  observed win rate may fall below the 34 % projection. Tracked by the flip
  criteria, which require ≥20 %.
- **Observation-window bias.** The 3.3 h intake window was dominated by
  audit/batch sessions (`session=audit-…`), which are long and prefill-heavy;
  the 34 % retained-win projection is therefore a lower bound for interactive
  work and an upper bound for audit bursts. Hence the requirement for a ≥24 h
  pre-flip baseline before applying the change.
- **Restart cost.** Applying the change restarts the proxy and drops in-flight
  local state; schedule in a quiet window.
- **Scope-creep guard.** Extra opportunities found (e.g. lease-active budget,
  windowed metrics in `/llama/local/status`) are recorded as linked work items,
  not absorbed here.

## Related work

- Depends on: `LP-0MVIKPCSG002B0NL` (reservation endpoint — `completed`).
- Related: `LP-0MVIQ0EXV00673HO` (120 s → 60 s, the current baseline),
  `LP-0MVICD2YW004DJPV` (occupancy-aware guard; holds the win/loss
  distributions), `LP-0MVIQ0F8T002FS42` (guard on the direct path),
  `LP-0MSORQVK50012Q4D` (queue origin), `LP-0MTF6EVLW007PEHN` (the opposite
  move: raise caps), `LP-0MU4NACW9001WKBP` (cumulative queue counters removed —
  logs are the telemetry contract), `LP-0MVIPY7QX0027XVD` (epic: local tail
  latency), `WL-0MVIKRFP0005JDL8` (client reservation adoption — related, not
  blocking).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MTF6EVLW007PEHN** – Raise cheap-mode contention queue caps (wait 60->120s, depth 4->8) (completed)
- **LP-0MU4NACW9001WKBP** – Remove useless contention queue cumulative counters (completed)
- **LP-0MVDUN5CY009VD20** – Reserve free-tier request budget for in-progress sessions, cap the wait at 15s (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — matched: 0msorqvk50012q4d, 0mvicd2yw004djpv, 0mvikpcsg002b0nl, ac1, ac2 (+158 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts.txt` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4, ac9 (+148 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_nothink.txt` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4, ac9 (+148 more)

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (trigger).** Reservations shipped 2026-10-21 but no client sends them
  (0 `local_admission_reserve_claimed` in 24 h; `reserved_issued: 0`;
  `WL-0MVIKRFP0005JDL8` still `idea`). Wait for client adoption, decouple, or
  split? — **Answer (operator, 2026-10-22): B — decouple.** Sweep on queue
  economics alone; ticket counts become reporting (AC3), not a gate.
  Evidence: `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log*` 24 h scan; `/llama/local/status`
  reservation counters; `wl show WL-0MVIKRFP0005JDL8`. Agent recommendation was
  B; operator confirmed.
- **Q2 (target values).** 30 s / depth 2 (34 % of wins retained), 20 s / depth 1
  (24 %), or 45 s / depth 4 (60 %)? — **Answer (operator, 2026-10-22):
  A — 30 s / depth 2.** Justification: post-60 s win p50 39.5 s / p75 48.1 s,
  every loss already burning the full budget.
- **Q3 (lease-active waiters).** 95 of 142 full-budget losses are
  `reason=local_lease_active`: one global value, or a longer budget for that
  branch? — **Answer (operator, 2026-10-22): A — one global value**; record the
  lease-active split as a reporting dimension, revisit only if it stays
  material after the sweep.

# Goal (user story)

As an operator/agent, I want the client to receive SSE keep-alive frames
while a local request is still in its **strict prefill window** (before the
upstream first byte), so a long prefill is visibly alive instead of a silent
socket that the client cannot distinguish from a hang.

Discovered during LP-0MVIQ0G2M0006QF6 (epic LP-0MVIPY7QX0027XVD): the item's
AC2 asks for keep-alive frames during prefill "and they stop when the first
byte arrives", but the existing `stream_heartbeat_interval_seconds` (default
10 s, `data: {"type":"heartbeat",...}`) only flows **after** the upstream
SSE headers arrive. For this llama.cpp build the headers arrive with the
first token, so the strict prefill window (the dominant tail: baseline 48 of
606 local dispatches had a first byte after >120 s, max 592 s) is completely
silent to the client.

## Why it was split out

`proxy_to_local` awaits `_await_first_byte_with_prefill_monitor` **before**
constructing the `StreamingResponse`, so no bytes can reach the client until
the upstream first byte. Emitting frames earlier needs the local dispatch to
return a streaming response *first* and move the first-byte wait into the
generator — a restructure of a large, delicate function that owns the lease
and slot lifecycle. Doing it under schedule pressure in the parent item would
have risked the tail it is meant to fix.

## Proposed change

1. For streaming requests, return a `StreamingResponse` immediately on the
   local path and perform the first-byte wait inside the generator, so
   keep-alive frames can be written while waiting.
2. Emit SSE comment frames (`: keep-alive` or `: prefill <pct>`) on a
   configurable cadence (reuse/clarify `stream_heartbeat_interval_seconds`
   or add `local_prefill_heartbeat_seconds`), stopping as soon as the first
   byte is forwarded.
3. Frames must be valid SSE comments for pi/opencode/curl and must not be
   counted as content by token accounting or by the content-delivered
   re-route boundary in `_preflight_streaming_response`.
4. Leases: the moved wait must keep the existing prefill-lease extension,
   the prefill deadline (LP-0MVIQ0G2M0006QF6) and the fail-closed orphan rule
   (LP-0MVIQ0FJC000YLX0) intact.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A local prefill longer than the cadence emits keep-alive frames at the
   configured cadence **before** the upstream first byte (test asserting the
   frame sequence with a stalled-upstream stub).
2. Frames stop when the first byte arrives and never leak into the response
   body/token accounting (test asserting no frame appears after content).
3. The content-delivered re-route boundary is unaffected (no pre-content
   frame may suppress recovery re-routing).
4. Lease/slot accounting and the prefill deadline still behave as tested in
   LP-0MVIQ0G2M0006QF6 / LP-0MVIQ0FJC000YLX0.
5. Malformed cadence config falls back to a safe default; docs updated.
6. Full test suite green; commit + hash recorded.

## Related work

- LP-0MVIQ0G2M0006QF6 — parent (deadline + ordering landed; this is its AC2).
- LP-0MVIPY7QX0027XVD — epic.
- LP-0MUXQ5QL40027VZ4 / LP-0MUXTW4MD003TVIC — prefill observability limits.
data.title: Emit SSE heartbeat frames during the strict prefill window (before upstream first byte)

# Goal (bug)

As an operator, I want a change to `models.ini` or `start-llama.sh` (model launch arguments: `ubatch-size`, `batch-size`, `ctx-size`, cache types, …) to force a llama-server restart on `start-proxy.sh --restart`, so a config edit is never silently left inactive.

## Evidence (2026-10-22, LP-0MVIQ0FSX006HQOS)

Setting `ubatch-size = 2048` in `models.ini` [Qwen3] and `UBATCH_SIZE=2048` / `LLAMA_UBATCH_SIZE:=2048` in `start-llama.sh`, then running `scripts/start-proxy.sh --restart`, left llama-server running with `--ubatch-size 1024`. Cause: the preserve decision hashes only the merged `config.yaml`

```
_restart_sha=$(merged_config_sha256(config.yaml, <overlay>))
# compared with .llama_server_signature.json config_sha256
if [ "$_sig_sha" = "$_restart_sha" ]; then KEEP_LLAMA=1; fi
```

`models.ini` and `start-llama.sh` are the actual launch-argument sources (the startup log even prints `BATCH_SIZE=…`), but they are not part of the signature, so any edit to them is invisible to the restart decision.

Workaround used at the time: delete `proxy/.llama_server_signature.json` to force `KEEP_LLAMA=0`. That is undocumented and easy to get wrong (the file lives under `proxy/`, not the repo root, although the script computes `REPO_ROOT` as the parent of `proxy/`).

## Proposed change

1. Include the model-launch inputs in the restart signature: hash `models.ini` and `start-llama.sh` (and any other launch-argument source the script reads) alongside the merged config.
2. Surface the reason in the startup log, e.g. `Restarting llama-server: models.ini changed since last start`, next to the existing preserve message.
3. Document the forced-restart escape hatch (`--force-llama-server` flag or removing the signature file) in the start-proxy skill and README.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Editing `models.ini` (e.g. a comment-only change and a value change, tested separately) followed by `start-proxy.sh --restart` restarts llama-server (test or documented manual verification with the observed argv).
2. Editing `start-llama.sh` likewise restarts llama-server.
3. An unchanged config/models.ini/start-llama.sh trio still preserves the warm llama-server (no regression to LP-0MUCEFCL6001ZXYN).
4. The startup log names which input changed.
5. The forced-restart path is documented in the start-proxy skill and `proxy/README.md`.
6. Full test suite green; commit + hash recorded.

## Related work

- LP-0MVIQ0FSX006HQOS — the ubatch A/B where this was hit (reverted; commit c9a49039).
- LP-0MUCEFCL6001ZXYN — the original "preserve the warm llama-server on a proxy-only restart" decision this must not regress.
- LP-0MVAPNC2900145RH — restart-reason plumbing in the same script.
data.title: llama-server restart signature ignores models.ini and start-llama.sh changes

# Intake brief: run the idle-admission measurement window

## Goal (user story)

As the operator, I want the idle-aware local admission override enabled for one
full ≥24 h window and analysed with `scripts/idle_admit_impact.py`, so
LP-0MVGHXD59008UOUD's AC1–AC5 can be resolved (enable by default, or record
the tuning) with measured numbers instead of a counterfactual estimate.

## Why this is a separate item

LP-0MVGHXD59008UOUD landed the measurement tooling (commit `c99ac884`):
`scripts/idle_admit_impact.py`, the `priority=`/`estimated_tokens=` dispatch
fields, `docs/dev/idle-window-measurements.md` and the config documentation.
What it cannot do is satisfy its own ACs, because the override is **off by
default** (`server.local_idle_admit_enabled: false`) and zero
`routing_idle_admit` events exist in any logged window. Enabling it changes live
routing, and the 24 h window cannot elapse inside a session — hence this item.

## Steps

1. Decide whether to enable the override for the window (live routing change:
   idle GPU time is spent on economic bypasses instead of paid remote calls,
   at the risk of a long first byte on an idle-admitted 120 K prompt).
2. Set `server.local_idle_admit_enabled: true` (keep
   `server.local_idle_admit_seconds: 60` for the first window), restart the
   proxy via `/skill:start-proxy --restart`, and record the restart timestamp.
3. Wait ≥ 24 h (the window cannot be shortened).
4. Run:
   `python3 scripts/idle_admit_impact.py --before-start '<baseline 24 h>' --before-end '<...>' --after-start '<restart>' --after-end '<+24 h>' --deployed-at '<restart>' --window-closed --json > /tmp/idle_admit_24h.json`
   plus `--markdown` for the report section.
5. Record the numbers + verdict on LP-0MVGHXD59008UOUD, then apply the AC5
   recommendation: keep the flag on (`enable_by_default`), or open the tuning
   follow-up the tool proposes and set the flag accordingly.

## Notes

- The baseline of record is 2026-10-19 07:23 → 2026-10-20 07:23 (table in the
  parent item and in `docs/dev/idle-window-measurements.md`).
- The counterfactual estimate over 2026-10-21 19:00 → 2026-10-22 19:00 was 937
  of 1,235 economic bypasses (75.9 %) with ≥ 60 s of system-wide local idle —
  the expected size of the win, not a measurement.
- Batch with LP-0MVGGPSVM003W35K (restored-prefix warmness, also waiting on a
  24 h post-deploy window) to avoid two separate experimental windows.
- `proxy-usage-analysis` reports the same override from the other side; use its
  05:00 daily report as the AC1 artifact of record when convenient.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The override has run for ≥ 24 h with `local_idle_admit` events > 0, and the
   window start is recorded (post-restart).
2. `scripts/idle_admit_impact.py --window-closed` runs clean on the window and
   its JSON artifact is attached to LP-0MVGHXD59008UOUD.
3. The AC1–AC4 numbers are recorded on LP-0MVGHXD59008UOUD next to the
   2026-10-19/20 baseline.
4. The AC5 outcome is decided and recorded: either `enable_by_default` (flag
   stays on) or the tuning follow-up (threshold / prompt-size cap / priority
   gating) is filed with the measured evidence.


## Key Files

- `proxy/config.yaml`
- `docs/dev/idle-window-measurements.md`
data.title: Run the idle-aware local admission >=24h measurement window

# Instrument and fix the slot sidecar seed path (restored-prefix warmness never fires)

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want the restored-prefix credit (LP-0MVGD9YXH008O304) to
actually fire for sessions that resume with a persisted slot snapshot, so the
feature is measurable — and if it cannot fire for the common case, I want to
know why with instrumentation instead of silence.

## Problem statement

The ≥24 h measurement (LP-0MVGGPSVM003W35K, 2026-10-22) found the seeding path
made **zero contact** in a 54.4 h post-deploy window:

- 0 `slot_ratio_restored` events, 0 `cache_state=restored` lines;
- the sidecar writer is healthy: 37 `slot_<session>.bin.ratio.json` sidecars
  written (2026-10-20 13:27 → 2026-10-22 19:43), names match the reader's
  candidate layout (`slot-cache/localhost-8080/`);
- 33 sessions with sidecars reached the local routing gate 2,918 times after
  their sidecar existed (including right after proxy restarts when the in-memory
  ratio was empty) and were still scored `cache_state=cold` — e.g. session
  `herdr-1792667491-…` (sidecar: 276 messages, saved 14:13) scored
  `cached_ratio=0.00 cache_state=cold messages=696` at 19:30 after a restart.

Root-cause suspects (in order of likelihood): (1) the `prefix_matches` guard
fails on real resumed conversations — first message (system prompt) regenerated
per request, and/or client-side compaction rewriting the front of the history
(proxy-side compaction is disabled: `compaction_bypass_eval … reason=compaction_disabled`);
(2) sidecars only exist for old snapshots, so a 24 h TTL plus front-rewrites
leaves no credit window; (3) (checked, unlikely) endpoint string drift between
save and seed. Seed outcomes log at DEBUG only, invisible at the INFO level the
proxy runs at.

## Split at producer request (2026-10-22)

The producer chose **instrument first**. The observability half is now its own S
child, **LP-0MVJYZWWW005XGW7** (INFO-level `slot_ratio_seed outcome=…` logging +
tests + docs), and this item depends on it. Do not change the credit logic
(`prefix_matches`, the sidecar TTL, the sidecar format) until the interface has
produced one traffic cycle of outcome counts: a fix attempted without that data
is guesswork. Effort below (M) covers the remaining fix plus the ≥24 h
re-measurement; priority is medium while it waits on data.

## Proposed change

1. Using the instrumented outcome counts, decide which failure mode is real:
   too-strict `prefix_matches` (rewritten system prompt / client-compacted
   history), an expired sidecar (24 h TTL vs long-lived sessions), or a lookup
   miss. Record the decision and the supporting data on this item.
2. Fix only the confirmed cause, consistent with AC2 of LP-0MVGD9YXH008O304 (a
   *changed* prompt still earns nothing; a *reusable prefix* must earn credit).
   Candidate approaches to evaluate: fingerprint the non-system messages only;
   anchor on a stable prompt-prefix hash; credit the last-saved overlapping
   messages; or compare against the last K messages of the stored list instead
   of requiring a prefix. Re-evaluate the TTL if it is the binding constraint.
3. Add a unit test reproducing the real resume pattern (sidecar saved for a full
   conversation; resumed request arrives with a rebuilt system prompt or a
   compacted front) that fails before the fix and passes after it.
4. Re-run the ≥24 h before/after measurement with
   `scripts/analyse_slot_ratio_restore.py` (built by LP-0MVGGPSVM003W35K):
   post-fix `cache_state=restored` dispatches must be > 0, and seeded dispatches
   must beat cold dispatches in the same context bucket (sample counts +
   percentiles).
5. Document the changed guard in `proxy/docs/routing.md`.

## Acceptance criteria

- A written verdict on this item names the confirmed failure mode and cites the instrumented outcome counts that prove it.
- For the confirmed cause, a unit test reproduces the resume-with-rewritten-front case and fails on the pre-fix code.
- After the fix, a ≥24 h window contains `cache_state=restored` dispatches, and their `dispatch_to_first_byte_ms` percentiles are stated against cold dispatches in the same context bucket with sample counts.
- No regression on AC2/AC3 of LP-0MVGD9YXH008O304 (mismatched snapshots earn nothing; restored ratio ≤ measured × margin).
- `proxy/docs/routing.md` documents the resolved guard and its failure modes.

## Risks / notes

- The 24 h TTL (`session_slot_ratio_ttl_seconds`) may itself be too short for
  the resume pattern observed (sidecar at 276 messages, resume at 696); include
  TTL in the investigation.
- Attribution caveat: the local-prefill improvement in the measurement window
  came from other changes (expected-reuse credit, admission ordering); do not
  use it as evidence for this path.

## Traceability

- discovered-from: LP-0MVGGPSVM003W35K (the AC5 measurement that found zero seeds)
- implementation of: LP-0MVGD9YXH008O304 (restored slot-prefix warmness)
- blocked by: LP-0MVJYZWWW005XGW7 (seed-outcome instrumentation)
- report: docs/dev/slot-prefix-warmness-measurement-LP-0MVGGPSVM003W35K.md

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/proxy/slot_cache_ratio.py` — the seed path and its guard: `prefix_matches()`,
  `seed_cached_ratio()` (validation order: snapshot → sidecar → model → TTL → prefix),
  `ttl_seconds()` / `_is_expired()`. The confirmed-cause fix lands here.
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — `expected_cached_ratio()` applies the *same*
  `prefix_matches` guard to the in-memory expected-reuse credit (~L812); a guard change
  must be evaluated for both call sites, not just the sidecar.
- `proxy/tests/test_slot_cache_ratio_restore.py` — add the resume-with-rewritten-front
  reproducer alongside the existing guard/TTL tests.
- `proxy/docs/routing.md` — restored-prefix warmness section (~L475–530): document the
  resolved guard and its failure modes.
- `scripts/analyse_slot_ratio_restore.py` — the AC3 re-measurement.
- `docs/dev/slot-prefix-warmness-measurement-LP-0MVGGPSVM003W35K.md` — the baseline the
  re-measurement is compared against.

## Plan (features and implementation tasks, 2026-10-22)

The five acceptance criteria decompose into three independently deliverable
slices plus the prerequisite instrumentation, in dependency order (verification
slices before implementation, per the plan skill's test-first rule):

| # | Work item | Type | Covers | Depends on |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **LP-0MVJYZWWW005XGW7** — Instrument slot-sidecar seed outcomes at INFO | task (S, risk Low) | prerequisite data (INFO `slot_ratio_seed outcome=…`) | — |
| 1 | **LP-0MVK0E8C40035FG3** — Diagnose the seed failure mode from outcome counts | task (verification) | AC1 | item 0 |
| 2 | **LP-0MVK0E80C009HUQC** — Fix the confirmed seed guard and document it | bug (test-first slice) | AC2, AC4, AC5 | item 1 |
| 3 | **LP-0MVK0E8NH007XCV3** — Re-measure restored vs cold over ≥24 h after the fix | task (verification) | AC3 | item 2 |

**Why three slices:** AC1 needs the instrumentation's outcome counts (a
traffic-cycle wait), and AC3 needs a ≥24 h post-fix window (another wait).
Neither wait can complete inside a single fix run, so each is its own item
with its own worktree lifecycle; the fix itself stays one vertical slice
(code + failing-then-passing test + docs) rather than being split
horizontally.

**Deliberately undecided:** the fix technique (non-system fingerprinting, a
stable prompt-prefix anchor, last-K overlap credit, or a TTL change) is chosen
from the diagnosis verdict, not here — the producer's "instrument first" split
stands. A fix attempted without the outcome counts is guesswork.

**Between phases:** after the diagnosis verdict lands, re-read the fix item's
description and update it so the reproducer test and the guard change match
the confirmed mode; after the fix lands, confirm the deployed build before the
re-measurement window starts.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MVJYZWWW005XGW7** – Instrument slot-sidecar seed outcomes at INFO (measure before fixing) (open)
- **LP-0MVGGPSVM003W35K** – Measure restored slot-prefix warmness impact over >=24h (before/after) (completed)
- **LP-0MVI2XOTY008Q4UV** – Second-turn cached_ratio scored 0.00 after a successful cold first local turn (bootstrap defect in update_cached_ratio) (completed)

### Repository file matches (verified by inspection)
- `proxy/proxy/slot_cache_ratio.py` — `prefix_matches()` (the suspected guard), `seed_cached_ratio()` validation order, `ttl_seconds()` / `_is_expired()` (TTL), `_candidate_slot_filenames()` (lookup)
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — `expected_cached_ratio()` reuses the same `prefix_matches` guard for the in-memory expected-reuse credit (~L812), so any guard change affects both paths; `_last_prompt_prefix` store
- `proxy/tests/test_slot_cache_ratio_restore.py` — existing guard/TTL tests (`test_changed_system_prompt_does_not_match`, `test_front_truncated_history_does_not_match`, `test_expired_sidecar_earns_no_credit`, `test_ttl_zero_disables_expiry`) to extend with the resume-with-rewritten-front case
- `proxy/docs/routing.md` — restored-prefix warmness section (~L475–530) to update
- `scripts/analyse_slot_ratio_restore.py` — ≥24 h before/after re-measurement tool
- `docs/dev/slot-prefix-warmness-measurement-LP-0MVGGPSVM003W35K.md` — baseline figures and sidecar inventory to compare against

## Intake notes (verification pass, 2026-10-22)

- **No interview required.** The seed brief already carried a problem statement with
  evidence, five measurable acceptance criteria, scoped constraints ("do not change the
  credit logic until the instrumentation has produced one traffic cycle"), risks and
  traceability; the remaining questions are answerable from the repo, which was read
  during this pass (seed path, guard, tests, docs, measurement report).
- **Duplicate check performed** (`wl search` on "slot sidecar restored prefix warmness"):
  no duplicate item exists. Related, non-overlapping items are the completed implementation
  LP-0MVGD9YXH008O304, the completed measurement LP-0MVGGPSVM003W35K (which triggered this
  item), the open instrumentation child LP-0MVJYZWWW005XGW7 and the completed
  expected-reuse credit LP-0MVI2XOTY008Q4UV.
- **Assumption (recorded, not decided):** the failure mode is not chosen here. The
  producer's "instrument first" split stands — this item stays `blocked` on
  LP-0MVJYZWWW005XGW7 and its fix is selected from the instrumented outcome counts.
- **Note on the shared guard:** because `prefix_matches` is also used by
  `provider.expected_cached_ratio()` for the in-memory expected-reuse credit, any guard
  change is a two-call-site change; the AC2 unit test must therefore assert the sidecar

# Fix the confirmed seed guard and document it

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want a resumed session whose conversation actually continues
a persisted slot snapshot to earn the restored-prefix routing credit, while a
genuinely changed prompt still earns nothing — so the restored-prefix feature
(LP-0MVGD9YXH008O304) is measurable instead of silently dead.

## Why (evidence)

LP-0MVGGPSVM003W35K found zero `cache_state=restored` dispatches in 54.4 h
despite healthy sidecar writing; LP-0MVJXV0MY000O77E AC1 (via its diagnosis
child) names the confirmed failure mode from the instrumented
`slot_ratio_seed outcome=…` counts. This item applies the minimal change that
makes the common resume pattern earn credit while preserving the AC2/AC3
guards of LP-0MVGD9YXH008O304.

## Scope

**In scope:** the confirmed-cause change to the seed guard (and/or the sidecar
TTL) in `proxy/proxy/slot_cache_ratio.py`, evaluated at **both** call sites,
plus the red→green reproducer test and the `routing.md` update. **Out of
scope:** any change not needed for the confirmed cause, re-running the
measurement (sibling item), and any change to the sidecar schema version or
the fail-open behaviour.

## Proposed change

1. **Test-first:** write the unit test reproducing the confirmed pattern in
   `proxy/tests/test_slot_cache_ratio_restore.py` — sidecar saved for a full
   conversation, resumed request arriving with a rebuilt system prompt or a
   front-compacted history (whatever the verdict named). Run it against the
   pre-fix code, capture the failing (red) output in a comment on this item,
   then make it pass with the fix.
2. Implement the smallest fix that credits the reusable prefix and still
   refuses a genuinely changed prompt, e.g. fingerprint the non-system
   messages only, anchor on a stable prompt-prefix hash, credit the
   last-saved overlapping messages, or compare against the last K stored
   fingerprints. Preserve the ratio cap (`min(1.0, cached/estimated) ×
   margin`), the sidecar schema version, and fail-open.
3. Evaluate the same guard change at the **second call site** —
   `provider.expected_cached_ratio()` (~L812) uses `prefix_matches` for the
   in-memory expected-reuse credit. Apply the change consistently there and
   assert a genuinely changed prompt still earns nothing (AC4 of the parent).
4. Re-evaluate the TTL only if the diagnosis proved it binding: either keep
   it, change the default in `ttl_seconds()`, or relax the check per the
   verdict's `age_s` evidence — with the number recorded in this item.
5. Update the restored-prefix warmness section of `proxy/docs/routing.md`
   (~L475–530): the resolved guard, what still earns nothing, the failure
   modes, and the config knobs that affect them.
6. Run the changed-scope test gate through the test skill; record the green
   result in a comment.

## Acceptance criteria

- The reproducer unit test matches the confirmed resume pattern, fails on the pre-fix code (red output captured in a comment), and passes after the fix.
- No regression on AC2/AC3 of LP-0MVGD9YXH008O304: a mismatched snapshot earns nothing and the restored ratio stays ≤ measured × safety margin — the existing cap and prefix tests (`TestRatioCap`, `test_changed_system_prompt_does_not_match`, `test_front_truncated_history_does_not_match`) stay green.
- A genuinely changed prompt still earns nothing: the existing `test_changed_system_prompt_does_not_match` and `test_front_truncated_history_does_not_match` expectations hold for the final guard, and the in-memory expected-reuse path (`provider.expected_cached_ratio()`) refuses the same diverged prompt.
- Sidecar schema version, sidecar format, fail-open behaviour, and seed success logging (`slot_ratio_restored`) are unchanged; no new config key is introduced unless the TTL change required one, in which case the default and its numerical justification are recorded here and in `routing.md`.
- `proxy/docs/routing.md` describes the resolved guard, what still earns nothing, and the failure modes, consistent with the parent's AC5.
- All changes land in the worktree of this item and pass the changed-scope test gate (build → test → commit order).

## Risks / notes

- The shared-guard note (parent intake notes): any `prefix_matches` change is
  a **two-call-site** change; the sidecar path test must be paired with the
  expected-reuse path assertion or the in-memory credit silently inherits a
  looser/different rule.
- Do not over-fit to the sample: the fix must generalise to a *reusable
  prefix* and still deny a *changed* prompt (AC2 of LP-0MVGD9YXH008O304), not
  just make the observed session pass.
- The ≥24 h re-measurement that proves the fix belongs to the sibling
  re-measurement item; do not conflate this item's green test gate with field
  confirmation.

## Traceability

- child of: LP-0MVJXV0MY000O77E (covers its AC2, AC4, AC5)
- blocked by: the diagnosis verdict (AC1 of LP-0MVJXV0MY000O77E)
- implementation of: LP-0MVGD9YXH008O304 (restored slot-prefix warmness)
- discovered-from: LP-0MVGGPSVM003W35K

## Key Files (verified by inspection, 2026-10-22)

- `proxy/proxy/slot_cache_ratio.py` — the guard and TTL live here:

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — `expected_cached_ratio()` (~L812) reuses

# Diagnose the seed failure mode from outcome counts

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want the instrumented `slot_ratio_seed outcome=…` counts
turned into a written verdict that names **the** failure mode behind zero
restored-prefix credits, so the fix on LP-0MVJXV0MY000O77E is chosen from data
instead of guesswork.

## Why (evidence)

LP-0MVGGPSVM003W35K measured a 54.4 h post-deploy window with **0**
`slot_ratio_restored` seeds and **0** `cache_state=restored` dispatches, while
37 `slot_<session>.bin.ratio.json` sidecars were written and 33
sidecar-bearing sessions reached the local routing gate **2,918** times
(including immediately after proxy restarts, when the in-memory ratio was
empty). The producer therefore split the work: LP-0MVJYZWWW005XGW7 adds
INFO-level outcome logging (behaviour-neutral), and this item turns those
counts into the verdict the fix depends on.

The three candidate modes, in the order recorded at intake:

1. **prefix mismatch** — `prefix_matches()` rejects real resumed
   conversations (system prompt regenerated per request, and/or client-side
   compaction rewriting the front of the history);
2. **expired sidecar** — the 24 h `session_slot_ratio_ttl_seconds` is shorter
   than the save→resume interval of long-lived sessions;
3. **lookup miss** — the candidate snapshot/sidecar path resolves differently
   at seed time than at save time (recorded as unlikely: the directory names
   matched).

## Scope

**In scope:** analysis of proxy logs plus a written verdict on
LP-0MVJXV0MY000O77E. **Out of scope:** any change to the credit logic,
`prefix_matches`, the sidecar TTL, the sidecar format, or `cached_ratio`
scoring — the fix belongs to the sibling item.

## Proposed change

1. After LP-0MVJYZWWW005XGW7 is deployed and has served at least one traffic
   cycle (target ≥24 h), aggregate the `slot_ratio_seed outcome=…` lines from
   `/var/log/llama-proxy` using the aggregation recipe documented in
   `proxy/docs/routing.md`. Record the exact command and the per-outcome
   counts (including `found`) on LP-0MVJXV0MY000O77E.
2. For the dominant skip outcome, correlate the logged
   `stored_messages` / `incoming_messages` / `age_s` fields:
   - `prefix_mismatch` — compare the stored vs incoming message counts and
     identify *where* the fronts diverge (rebuilt system prompt versus
     front-compacted history); state how many of the sampled sessions show
     each pattern;
   - `expired` — tabulate the `age_s` distribution so a replacement TTL can be
     justified numerically;
   - `missing_snapshot` / `missing_sidecar` — confirm whether the session
     truly had no saved snapshot or whether the candidate lookup drifted, and
     record the candidate list if it is logged.
3. Write the verdict as a comment on LP-0MVJXV0MY000O77E: the confirmed mode,
   the count share that proves it, why the other two modes are ruled out (with
   their own counts), and which candidate fix it implies (fingerprint the
   non-system messages only / stable prompt-prefix anchor / credit the last
   saved overlapping messages / re-evaluate the TTL default).
4. If the counts are inconclusive (too little traffic, instrumentation gap, or
   a mode outside the three suspects), record that honestly, keep the fix item
   blocked, and file a follow-up item with the evidence instead of guessing.

## Acceptance criteria

- Per-outcome `slot_ratio_seed` counts over a window of at least one full traffic cycle (target ≥24 h) are recorded on LP-0MVJXV0MY000O77E together with the exact aggregation command used.
- A written verdict on this item (LP-0MVJXV0MY000O77E) names the confirmed failure mode and cites the instrumented `slot_ratio_seed` outcome counts that prove it, with the count share; the two alternative modes are explicitly ruled out using their own counts.
- The verdict names the candidate fix it implies and explains why that fix still satisfies AC2 of LP-0MVGD9YXH008O304 (a genuinely changed prompt earns nothing).
- Where the confirmed mode is `expired`, the verdict includes the observed `age_s` distribution, so any TTL change is numerically justified.
- No change to the credit logic is made in this item: `git diff` over `proxy/proxy/` is empty for the credit paths (this is a verification-only item).
- If the counts are inconclusive, the item's closing comment says so, the fix item stays blocked, and a follow-up item is created with the evidence.

## Risks / notes

- Snapshot-bearing traffic is thin (2,918 gated decisions from 33 sessions in
  54 h); a single 24 h window may not sample every outcome. Extend the window
  rather than concluding from a handful of lines.
- The verdict must not be influenced by the unrelated local-prefill
  improvement recorded in the baseline report (attribution caveat on
  LP-0MVJXV0MY000O77E).
- If the instrumentation turns out to be missing lines for the common case,
  treat that as an instrumentation defect (follow-up item), not as evidence
  about the guard.

## Traceability

- discovered-from: LP-0MVGGPSVM003W35K (measurement that found zero seeds)
- child of: LP-0MVJXV0MY000O77E (covers its AC1)
- blocked by: LP-0MVJYZWWW005XGW7 (INFO `slot_ratio_seed outcome=…`
  instrumentation)
- blocks: the guard/TTL fix (its sibling) and the post-fix re-measurement

## Key Files (verified by inspection, 2026-10-22)

- `proxy/docs/routing.md` — the outcome vocabulary and the documented
  aggregation recipe (added by LP-0MVJYZWWW005XGW7); the source of truth for
  how to count outcomes.
- `scripts/analyse_slot_ratio_restore.py` — the existing measurement tool
  (windows, `cache_state` tables, sidecar inventory); reuse its window handling
  rather than hand-grepping where possible.
- `docs/dev/slot-prefix-warmness-measurement-LP-0MVGGPSVM003W35K.md` — the
  zero-seed baseline this verdict is compared against.
- `proxy/proxy/slot_cache_ratio.py` — read-only reference for the validation
  order (`snapshot → sidecar → model → TTL → prefix`) so each outcome maps to
  the branch that produced it.

# Re-measure restored vs cold over ≥24 h after the fix

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want a ≥24 h post-fix window that proves the restored-prefix
credit actually fires (`cache_state=restored` dispatches exist) and that it
pays for itself (seeded dispatches beat cold dispatches in the same context
bucket), so AC3 of LP-0MVJXV0MY000O77E is answered with real numbers.

## Why (evidence)

The baseline (LP-0MVGGPSVM003W35K) recorded **0** `cache_state=restored`
dispatches in 54.4 h and **0** `slot_ratio_restored` seeds — so the fix item's
green test gate is not enough; the field measurement is the acceptance test.
The pre-fix local-prefill improvement in that window was caused by other
changes (expected-reuse credit, admission ordering) and must not be used as
evidence for this path (attribution caveat on the parent item).

## Scope

**In scope:** deploying nothing new (the fix item's build), waiting out a
≥24 h window, and producing the before/after comparison with
`scripts/analyse_slot_ratio_restore.py`. **Out of scope:** changing the seed
path again if the window shows zero restored dispatches — that reopens the
diagnosis with the new evidence rather than silently tweaking the guard.

## Proposed change

1. Confirm the fix build (the sibling item's worktree merge) is the deployed
   proxy version, and note the deploy timestamp.
2. Wait out a ≥24 h window (per shared background-job etiquette: launch, do
   other work, then one completion-aware wait). Optionally aggregate the
   `slot_ratio_seed outcome=…` counts for the same window to cross-check the
   seed share.
3. Run `scripts/analyse_slot_ratio_restore.py` over the baseline window and
   the post-fix window (machine-readable `--json` output saved alongside the
   report).
4. State the verdict on LP-0MVJXV0MY000O77E:
   - `cache_state=restored` dispatch count and `slot_ratio_restored` seed
     count (>0 required);
   - restored-vs-cold `dispatch_to_first_byte_ms` p50/p90 with sample counts,
     same context bucket (reuse the bucket table layout from the baseline);
   - sidecar inventory at report time, and the `slot_save`/`slot_restore`
     confound rows.
5. Add the report (a section appended to
   `docs/dev/slot-prefix-warmness-measurement-LP-0MVGGPSVM003W35K.md` or a new
   file under `docs/dev/`) and link it from the parent item.
6. If the window still shows 0 restored dispatches, record the honest result,
   state the outcome counts that explain it (via the diagnosis item's
   aggregation recipe), and file a follow-up — do not claim success.

## Acceptance criteria

- A post-fix window of ≥24 h contains more than zero `cache_state=restored` dispatches and more than zero `slot_ratio_restored` seed events, with the exact counts stated.
- `dispatch_to_first_byte_ms` percentiles (at least p50 and p90) for restored dispatches are stated against cold dispatches **in the same context bucket**, with sample counts for both groups.
- The same window's `slot_ratio_seed outcome=…` counts are aggregated, so the restored share is explainable from the seeding outcomes.
- A written report is added under `docs/dev/` (or appended to the baseline report) with the command line used, and is linked from LP-0MVJXV0MY000O77E.
- If restored dispatches are still zero, the verdict says so honestly, explains the outcome counts, and creates a follow-up item instead of claiming success.

## Risks / notes

- Snapshot-bearing traffic is thin (2,918 gated decisions / 54 h baseline);
  if a single day yields too few restored samples, extend the window and wait
  for a full traffic cycle rather than concluding early.
- The attribution caveat from the baseline applies in reverse too: a restored
  win must be attributed to the seeding path, not to unrelated local-prefill
  gains made in the same window.
- Schedule: this item cannot complete until the fix build has been deployed
  and exposed to ≥24 h of traffic — plan the wait, do not hold a slot during
  it.

## Traceability

- child of: LP-0MVJXV0MY000O77E (covers its AC3)
- blocked by: the guard/TTL fix (its sibling)
- uses: `scripts/analyse_slot_ratio_restore.py`
  (LP-0MVGGPSVM003W35K) and the instrumentation aggregate recipe
  (LP-0MVJYZWWW005XGW7)
- baseline compared against:
  `docs/dev/slot-prefix-warmness-measurement-LP-0MVGGPSVM003W35K.md`

## Key Files (verified by inspection, 2026-10-22)

- `scripts/analyse_slot_ratio_restore.py` — windows, `cache_state` tables,
  bucket pairs, sidecar inventory; run with `--json` and save the output.
- `docs/dev/slot-prefix-warmness-measurement-LP-0MVGGPSVM003W35K.md` — the

## Problem statement

Six `REFACTOR-<work-item-id>` provenance markers are still embedded in `proxy/` sources even though every referenced work item is **completed**. The refactor skill injects these markers when it files a smell (`remediate_pre_existing()` → `inject_refactor_comment()`) but nothing removes them when the item closes, so stale markers re-trigger refactor scans and re-file duplicate work items (LP-0MVIR51KL0096QOB was re-filed against an already-fixed F823 smell that LP-0MVJXC9MK003UET8 had resolved).

# Intake brief: idle admission is gated by foreign idle local leases

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want an idle-admitted request to be able to use genuinely
idle local capacity even when another session merely *holds* a local dispatch
lease that is doing no work, so the idle-admission override actually converts
`large_context_bypass` skips instead of being refused one gate later.

## Problem statement

`server.local_idle_admit_enabled` decides, in
`_evaluate_idle_admission_override`, that an economic `large_context_bypass`
should be served locally while the GPU is idle — but the dispatch path then
refuses on `local_lease_active` whenever another session holds the local
dispatch lease, and the bounded contention queue (`contention_queue_max_wait_seconds`,
60 s) cannot outlast a lease that has hundreds of seconds left. The admission
decision and the admission gate therefore disagree about what "idle" means.

## Finding (discovered during LP-0MVJXGSEG0045IAF)

Live probe on 2026-10-22 ~21:57 with the override enabled
(`server.local_idle_admit_enabled: true`):

- `/llama/local/status`: `local_idle_seconds=139`, `capacity_hint=idle`,
  `local_active_query=false` — i.e. the exact state the override targets.
- `local_owner_session_id` was an `audit-AH-…` session holding the local lease
  with ~705 s remaining.
- A ~45 k-token cold prompt (a `large_context_bypass`) was refused with
  `{"code":"no_slots_available","reason":"local_lease_active"}`; the projected
  wait exceeded the contention budget, so no admission and no local dispatch.

Mechanism: `provider._local_idle_blocker()` (the override's guard) checks
self-healing / model switch / backend health / active or generating queries /
prefill in flight / queue depth — it does **not** consider a foreign idle
lease. The dispatch path then refuses on `local_lease_active`
(`provider.py` ~9777) and queues only within
`contention_queue_max_wait_seconds`, so a long idle lease defeats the
admission decision.

### Log re-check at intake (2026-10-22 21:48–21:59, `proxy.log`)

The original finding conflates two different blocking shapes; they need
different treatment, and only the second can hold a lease for hundreds of
seconds. Evidence:

- **Lease lifetimes.** A finished request's cooldown lease is set from the
  **base** timeout only (`_decrement_local_active_queries` →
  `expires_at = now + _get_lease_timeout_seconds()`), which is
  `local_dispatch_lease_timeout_seconds: 30`. Hundreds of residual seconds can
  therefore only come from the **adaptive** lease attached at acquisition
  (`30 + estimated_tokens × 0.015`, cap `local_dispatch_max_prefill_seconds`
  = 900 s): `30 + 45,000 × 0.015 = 705` matches the observed figure exactly.
- **Observed state while a foreign lease blocked dispatching** (`status_request`
  lines, 21:57:00–21:59:23):
  `local_idle_seconds=39.9 → 182.8`, `local_active_query=true`,
  `available_slots=2`, `capacity_hint=idle`,
  `local_owner_session_id=audit-AH-0MVIMPC11001F7WU-…`,
  `local_owner_lease_remaining_seconds=143.6 → 0.7` — i.e. an **`active`**
  record with no GPU work behind it, holding the pool while
  `local_dispatch_denied … owner=… active=1` repeats.
  At 21:59:26 the record was reclaimed:
  `lease_released … reason=no_progress_watchdog` /
  `dispatch_cleanup removed 1 stale lease(s)`.
- **The idle clock is not prefill-aware.** `proxy/local_activity.py` updates it
  on dispatch start, first byte, every chunk and finish — not on prefill
  progress — so a long silent prefill also reports "idle" while
  `local_prefill_in_flight` is set.
- **Gate order.** In the wedge/prefill shape `_local_idle_blocker` returns
  `local_active` (via `local_active_queries > 0`) or `prefill_in_flight`
  *before* the request ever reaches the `local_lease_active` dispatch refusal.
  So "the override already decided to admit, then the lease gate refused it"
  is only true for the case where the counter says nothing is running.

Two blocking shapes, both in scope (operator decision Q1):

- **Shape A — inactive cooldown lease.** Owner finished; the record stays
  reserved for its session for the 30 s base cooldown (no-preemption policy).
  Bounded, small: it converts only the "frees in a few seconds" cases.
- **Shape B — `active` record whose owner is not working.** Either a wedged /
  abandoned stream (reclaimed by the 180 s no-progress watchdog, or at the
  900 s ceiling) or a long silent prefill. The adaptive lease can be hundreds
  of seconds, and the record also keeps `local_active_queries` /
  `local_prefill_in_flight` set, so the override is refused one gate earlier.

## Why it matters

- In this agent-heavy environment, sessions that think on a remote model while
  parked between turns hold local leases for minutes. That is precisely when the
  GPU is idle, so the override's benefit can be largely unrealisable.
- The counterfactual estimate for the measurement item (75.9 % of economic
  bypasses had >= 60 s of system-wide local idle) ignores leases by
  construction, so the measured conversion may land far below it. The
  measurement will quantify the gap; this item is about the mechanism.

## Users

- **Operator (primary):** "As the operator, I want a measured statement of how
  much of the idle-capacity win the lease gate costs, and a decision on whether
  to change the gate, so I can decide whether the override earns its default-on
  setting." (from LP-0MVJXGSEG0045IAF AC5)
- **Session holding the lease:** "As the session that owns a local lease, I want
  an idle-admitted request not to silently destroy my slot-prefix reuse without
  the cost being counted, so that my next turn is not unexpectedly slow."
- **Agent waiting for local capacity:** "As an agent whose request was bypassed,
  I want the idle-admission decision and the dispatch gate to agree, so a
  bypassed prompt does not wait 60 s in the contention queue and then fall back
  remotely anyway."

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1** — The measured conversion rate from LP-0MVJXGSEG0045IAF is quoted, and the lease-gate effect on it is stated in `docs/dev/idle-window-measurements.md` — including which of the two blocking shapes (A: inactive cooldown lease, B: `active` record with no work behind it) accounts for the refusals, from `local_dispatch_denied` / `lease_released` / `local_lease_active` counts in the measurement window.
- **AC2** — One of the options below is chosen with that evidence, and a follow-up implementation item is filed (or the "leave as is" decision recorded).
- **AC3** — If a gate change is chosen, the change is fail-safe: it can only convert a bypass the override already decided to admit, never widen admission for requests the guard refused.
- **AC4** — If a gate change is chosen, its eligibility predicate distinguishes a lease whose owner is **working** from one that is **not** (no `last_progress_ts` advance and the llama-server slot not processing), and the decision record states which shape(s) it converts. Unit tests cover: preempting a verified idle foreign lease, still refusing a genuinely working foreign lease, the inactive cooldown lease, a prefill in flight, and the unchanged `context_too_large` capacity cap.
- **AC5** — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (`docs/dev/idle-window-measurements.md`, `docs/dev/slot-management-design.md`, `proxy/README.md`, `proxy/config.yaml` knob comments as applicable).
- **AC6** — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Fail-safe by construction.** The change may only convert a bypass the
  override already decided to admit; it must never admit anything the guard
  refused (nor touch the physical `context_too_large` cap).
- **No silent re-prefill for the displaced owner.** A lease exists to protect
  slot-prefix reuse; preemption costs the owner a re-prefill. The chosen design
  must state that cost (and the log/measurement evidence for it), not just take
  the capacity.
- **No new restart requirement.** Routing-policy changes must not require a
  proxy/llama-server restart (LP-0MVDT94F0003VHUA AC4); any new knob is
  config-read at dispatch time or hot-reloadable via
  `POST /admin/reload-config`.
- **Default preserves today's behaviour** unless the measurement shows the
  conversion is material; a behaviour change ships behind a flag with the
  documented decision.
- **Evidence dependency.** AC1 needs the ≥24 h window that started
  2026-10-22 21:48 (LP-0MVJXGSEG0045IAF); this item cannot decide before it.

## Existing state

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — `_local_idle_blocker()` (~2410) lists the guard
  blockers but knows nothing about leases; `_evaluate_idle_admission_override`
  (2484) gates on it plus `local_idle_seconds`; `_local_concurrency_info`
  (~5054) and `_maybe_queue_for_local_slot` (~5655) bound the queue budget;
  the `local_lease_active` fallback branch is at ~9777.
- `proxy/proxy/router.py` — the `local_lease_active` 503 payload
  (`no_slots_available`, `local_owner_session_id`, `Retry-After`) is built at
  ~1240–1290.
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — `_try_acquire_local_dispatch` (1656) owns
  the no-preemption occupancy rule (active + inactive-unexpired foreign
  records count); `_decrement_local_active_queries` (1305) resets the record to
  `active=False` with the **base** cooldown; `_query_slot_processing` (1972)
  and `_cleanup_stale_local_dispatch` (2080) provide the slot-liveness and
  no-progress-wedge signals (180 s watchdog, 900 s max-prefill ceiling);
  `_release_local_dispatch` (1901) is the only path that frees a lease early.
- `proxy/proxy/local_activity.py` — the idle clock (not prefill-aware).
- `proxy/proxy/handlers.py` (~640–670) — `/llama/local/status` reports
  `local_owner_session_id` only for **active** records, plus
  `local_owner_lease_remaining_seconds`, so the probe's "idle lease" reading
  came from an `active` record.
- Config as shipped: `local_dispatch_lease_timeout_seconds: 30`,
  `local_dispatch_lease_per_token_seconds: 0.015` (cap 900 s via
  `local_dispatch_max_prefill_seconds`), `session_slot_pool_size: 2`,
  `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds: 60`, `local_idle_admit_seconds: 60`,
  `local_idle_admit_enabled: true` (measurement window).
- Existing tests to extend: `proxy/tests/test_local_idle_admission.py`,
  `test_local_dispatch_gate.py`, `test_generating_only_pool.py`,
  `test_recover_stuck_global_active_queries.py`, `test_contention_queue.py`,
  `test_llama_local_status.py`.

## Options (to be decided with the measured numbers)

1. **Leave as is** if the measured conversion is material — then just document
   the lease gate in `docs/dev/idle-window-measurements.md` as the reason the
   counterfactual over-estimates.
2. **Treat a foreign idle lease as non-blocking for idle admission** (i.e. let
   an idle-admitted request preempt / share an idle lease), bounded by the same
   "nothing queued/in flight" guard. Needs a lease-handover design (the lease
   exists to protect slot-prefix reuse, so preempting it may cost its owner a
   re-prefill). Blanket form: preempts even a working owner.
3. **Gate on lease remaining time** — admit only when the foreign lease is
   within the contention budget (small, safe change; converts the "frees in a
   few seconds" cases only, i.e. shape A).
4. **Preempt only foreign leases verified idle** (added at intake, Q2 = A) —
   reuse the existing liveness machinery as the eligibility predicate: no
   `last_progress_ts` advance within a short window **and** the recorded
   llama-server slot not `is_processing` (`_query_slot_processing`). This is
   the only option that can safely convert shape B: it releases a wedged or
   abandoned record immediately instead of waiting for the 180 s watchdog /
   adaptive expiry, and never displaces an owner that is actually prefilling or
   decoding.
5. **Fix the decision input instead of the gate** — only relevant if the
   measurement shows shape B is dominated by long silent prefills: make the
   idle signal prefill-aware so the override stops calling a busy prefill
   "idle". Out of scope unless the evidence points there; recorded so the
   decision can name it rather than rediscover it.

## Desired change

A recorded decision (one option, with the AC1 numbers), plus either a
"leave as is" note in `docs/dev/idle-window-measurements.md` or a filed
follow-up implementation item carrying the chosen mechanism, its fail-safe
predicate and the displaced-owner cost.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — `_local_idle_blocker` / override evaluation: add
  the lease-eligibility input or pass an "idle-admitted" marker to the dispatch
  gate.
- `proxy/proxy/router.py` — `local_lease_active` refusal path: honour the
  admitted marker when the foreign lease is verified idle.
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — `_try_acquire_local_dispatch` (occupancy /
  preemption) and `_query_slot_processing` (verified-idle predicate).
- `proxy/proxy/local_activity.py` — only if option 5 is chosen.
- `proxy/config.yaml` — any new knob plus its documented default.
- `docs/dev/idle-window-measurements.md`, `docs/dev/slot-management-design.md`,
  `proxy/README.md` — the decision and the measured lease effect.
- `proxy/tests/test_local_idle_admission.py` (extend) and
  `proxy/tests/test_local_dispatch_gate.py`.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Wrong input signal (shape B).** `local_idle_seconds` cannot see a silent
  prefill, so any design that trusts it alone may admit during real work; the
  guard's `prefill_in_flight` / `local_active` checks are what currently prevent
  that, and a lease change must not weaken them.
- **Displaced-owner cost.** Preempting an idle lease may cost its owner a
  re-prefill (minutes on a large prompt). Unmeasured today; must be stated in
  the decision, and is the reason option 4 restricts preemption to verified
  idle owners.
- **Wedge/orphan overlap.** Shape B includes abandoned streams. The
  no-progress watchdog (LP-0MUCEFB8E003YVFF) and orphan cleanup
  (LP-0MSUO6XRP001MCB2) already reclaim these after 180 s; option 4 makes that
  immediate *for the admission decision only* and must not duplicate or
  undermine their cleanup semantics.
- **Measurement may not settle it.** If the ≥24 h window yields too few
  idle-admitted samples (no `routing_idle_admit` event had been logged as of
  22:19), AC1 can only be answered qualitatively; record that explicitly
  instead of guessing.
- **Scope-creep risk.** Fixing audit-session lease hygiene (why an `active`
  record with no work exists for minutes) is a separate concern tracked by the
  wedge/orphan items; record such opportunities as linked work items, not as
  extra scope here.
- **Assumption:** the 705 s figure is an adaptive lease
  (`30 + 45,000 × 0.015`); the arithmetic matches but the owning record has not
  been confirmed from the log at the probe instant — see Appendix Q3.

## Related work

- **LP-0MVJXGSEG0045IAF** — *Run the idle-aware local admission ≥24 h measurement
  window* — blocks this item: its measured conversion rate and reason counts are
  the AC1 evidence.
- **LP-0MVGHXD59008UOUD** — *Measure idle-aware local admission impact over
  ≥24 h* — the measurement item whose AC5 decision (enable by default / tune)
  this mechanism finding has to inform.
- **LP-0MVGD9Z8Z0055Y5J** — the idle-admission override itself (guard +
  decision), the code this item's decision would adjust.
- **LP-0MU5BOMJM008F17C** — local lease denial falls through to remote instead
  of queueing; the fix that put `local_lease_active` through the contention
  queue (the 60 s budget this item's long leases defeat).
- **LP-0MVIQ0EXV00673HO** — contention-queue max wait lowered 120 s → 60 s;
  fixes the budget this item must reason against.
- **LP-0MUCEFB8E003YVFF** — no-progress watchdog that releases wedged `active`
  leases (observed reclaiming the probe's audit lease); option 4 must not
  duplicate its semantics.
- **LP-0MSUO6XRP001MCB2** — orphan cleanup verifies the slot against
  llama-server `/slots` before freeing a lease (the liveness predicate option 4
  would reuse).
- **LP-0MRB29PP60012UYF** — *Bug: Stale Local Dispatch Lease Blocks Subsequent
  Local Requests* — completed; closest precedent for the same failure shape
  (automated match).
- **LP-0MR9G183O004SJLO** — *Add local_owner_session_id to /llama/local/status*
  — completed; the field the original probe used to identify the lease owner
  (automated match).
- **LP-0MRDI0SOS002JBD0** — *Re-verify slot lease and retry cascade fixes* —
  completed; prior verification of the lease/retry interaction (automated
  match).
- **LP-0MVDT94F0003VHUA** — constrains the solution: routing-policy changes
  never restart the proxy or llama-server.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MR9G183O004SJLO** – Add local_owner_session_id to /llama/local/status endpoint (completed)
- **LP-0MRB29PP60012UYF** – Bug: Stale Local Dispatch Lease Blocks Subsequent Local Requests (completed)
- **LP-0MRDI0SOS002JBD0** – Re-verify slot lease and retry cascade fixes (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — the override guard and the lease-refusal branch
  (matches dominated by keyword frequency; the curated Key Files list above is
  authoritative).
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts*.txt` — corpus noise, not
  related.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (scope)** — "Should this item cover both blocking shapes (inactive
  cooldown leases *and* stale `active` records holding the pool while the GPU
  is idle), or only finished-inactive cooldown leases?"
  — **Answer (operator, interactive reply): (a) Both.** Also records the
  reasoning: the 705 s figure only makes sense for the second shape, so a
  cooldown-only item would solve a much smaller problem. Source: interactive
  reply, this intake session. Research: `proxy.log` 21:57–21:59 status lines,
  `router_helpers._decrement_local_active_queries` (base-only cooldown).
- **Q2 (option set)** — "Should a 4th option be added: preempt only foreign
  leases verified idle (no progress + llama-server slot not processing)?"
  — **Answer (operator, interactive reply): (a) Yes, add it.**
  Source: interactive reply, this intake session. Research: the eligibility
  signals already exist (`last_progress_ts`, `_query_slot_processing`,
  `_cleanup_stale_local_dispatch`).
- **Q3 (OPEN QUESTION, own research)** — "Is the probe's ~705 s lease an
  adaptive lease on an **active** record (and therefore shape B), and was it
  wedged or merely prefilling?"
  — Not yet confirmed. Evidence for the arithmetic: base 30 s +
  45,000 tokens × 0.015 = 705 s; `/llama/local/status` only reports
  `local_owner_session_id` for `active` records; a `no_progress_watchdog`
  release of exactly such an `active` audit lease is visible at 21:59:26.
  The AC1 window should settle it from `lease_released` reasons.

## Goal

Regenerate the four 24 h analysis windows with the existing `analyze_proxy_usage.py` CLI and archive the raw rotated log segments covering them, **before** retention rotates them away — so every number quoted in the investigation (AC1/AC2/AC6) stays reproducible after rotation.

This runs first, in parallel with the tooling children, because log retention is not contractual (parent constraint) and the base window's rotated segments are already ~4 days old.

## Scope

No skill-code changes: uses the CLI as-is. Archiving is copy-only; log data is never edited in place.

## Work

1. Confirm each window is still resolvable from `/var/log/llama-proxy` (log clock = local Europe/Dublin):

   | name | start | end |
   |---|---|---|
   | `base24` | 2026-10-18 14:37:48 | 2026-10-19 14:37:48 |
   | `ref24` | 2026-10-19 14:44:27 | 2026-10-20 14:44:27 |
   | `post24` | 2026-10-20 14:44:27 | 2026-10-21 14:44:27 |
   | `now24` | 2026-10-21 14:44:27 | 2026-10-22 14:44:27 |

2. Run the CLI once per window:

   ```
   python3 .pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py \
     --log-dir /var/log/llama-proxy --start "<start>" --end "<end>" \
     --output-dir "$HOME/proxy-usage-reports/cost/<name>"
   ```

3. Archive raw segments covering 2026-10-18 00:00 → 2026-10-22 23:59 (`proxy.log-2026-10-1[89]_*.gz`, `proxy.log.2026-10-1[89]_*.gz`, `proxy.log-2026-10-2[012]*`, `proxy.log.2026-10-2[012]*`, `proxy.log`, plus the matching `llama-server.log*`) into `$HOME/proxy-usage-reports/cost/raw/`, preserving the originals and verifying each copy with `gzip -t` (or `cmp`) after copy. Total is ~26 MB, so a full copy is cheap.

4. Write `$HOME/proxy-usage-reports/cost/raw/manifest.txt` recording, per window: the start/end boundary, the exact CLI command used, the output dir, and the headline numbers printed by the CLI (sessions, requests, logged tokens) so the parent's recorded figures can be checked against a committed command (AC6).

5. Post a comment on the parent with the archive path, the manifest path, and the four headline rows.

## Expected outcome

Four regenerated window directories plus a raw archive and manifest, so later children (and any future re-measurement) do not depend on log retention.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `~/proxy-usage-reports/cost/{base24,ref24,post24,now24}/` each contain `report.md`, `standard_sessions.csv`, `low_priority_sessions.csv`, and `errors.csv`/`errors.json`.
2. Every archived segment in `$HOME/proxy-usage-reports/cost/raw/` passes an integrity check after copy (`gzip -t`/`cmp`), and the originals under `/var/log/llama-proxy` are unmodified.
3. `manifest.txt` records, per window, the start/end boundary and the exact CLI command that produced the output.
4. `base24` and `post24` reproduce the parent's headline figures (421.7 M → 828.5 M logged tokens, 12,810 → 9,137 requests) within ±5%; any larger discrepancy is recorded with the CLI values that differ rather than silently accepted.
5. A parent comment links the archive and manifest paths, and every command used appears in the manifest.
6. No log file is edited or rewritten in place.

## Key Files

- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py` — used as-is for window regeneration
- `${HOME}/proxy-usage-reports/cost/raw/manifest.txt` — window boundaries + reproducible commands

## Notes

- `now24` is a fourth reference window (operator decision, plan Q1A) so a single before/after pair containing seven co-landed commits is not the only evidence.
- If a window has already rotated away, record that limitation in the parent comment and use the recorded figures from the parent description as the baseline (stated fallback per the parent's assumption).

## Goal

Pin the new per-dispatch prompt-size instrumentation with tests **before** implementation (test-first), so AC1's "per-dispatch `routing_check ... estimated_tokens` distributions" becomes a tested, deterministic CLI output instead of an ad-hoc `zgrep`/`awk` measurement.

## Scope

Tests and fixtures only. No production behaviour change in this item — the new tests are intentionally red until the implementation child lands (documented TDD convention, see LP-0MVF1FM9500070U1).

`routing_check` is **not parsed at all** today: `log_parser.py` handles `routing_idle_admit` (which shares the `estimated_tokens=`/`new_tokens=`/`cached_ratio=`/`cache_state=` fields) but nothing for `routing_check` itself.

## Work

1. Add fixture log lines to `tests/fixtures.py` mirroring the real format verbatim (sampled from `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log.2026-10-21_07.gz`):

   ```
   2026-10-21 03:51:45,845 - INFO - routing_check provider=local-qwen3 model=Qwen3 estimated_tokens=40741 cold_threshold=38000 warm_threshold=100000 new_tokens=2667 cached_ratio=0.93 cache_state=warm messages=23 session=herdr-1792545542-513674-2522 chain_hold_cycle=0
   ```

   Include at least: a warm/cold pair, a `chain_hold_cycle>0` line, a line with no `session=`, and one with a remote provider (`opencode-go`) so the distribution is not local-only.

2. Parser unit tests (`tests/test_llama_log_parser.py`): each line parses to an event carrying `provider`, `model`, `estimated_tokens`, `new_tokens`, `cached_ratio`, `cache_state`, `messages`, `session`, `chain_hold_cycle`; an incomplete line (e.g. missing `estimated_tokens=`) is skipped deterministically rather than raising or producing a partial event that inflates distributions.

3. Aggregation unit tests: count, median, mean and p90 of `estimated_tokens` (and `new_tokens`) over a fixture set, the warm/cold `cached_ratio` split, and mean `messages`.

4. End-to-end assertion (`tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py`): a CLI run over fixture logs emits the new report section and the per-dispatch CSV artifact with the expected values, and `summary_to_json` exposes the distribution.

5. Document, in the test module, that the assertions are intentionally red until the implementation child (mirroring the existing TDD convention used by `LP-0MVF1FM9500070U1`).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A parser unit test asserts all nine fields of a representative `routing_check` line, including `chain_hold_cycle`.
2. A unit test asserts an incomplete/malformed `routing_check` line is skipped deterministically (no exception, no partially-populated event).
3. An aggregation unit test asserts count/median/mean/p90 for `estimated_tokens` and `new_tokens`, plus warm/cold counts and mean `messages`, over a fixture set whose expected values are computed by hand in the test.
4. An end-to-end test asserts the report section and CSV artifact appear in a CLI run over fixture logs, with the expected distribution values.
5. Tests fail against the current code for the expected reason (missing event kind), and that intentional-red state is documented in the test module.
6. No production file is modified by this item.

## Key Files

- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/fixtures.py` — new `routing_check` fixture lines
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_llama_log_parser.py` — parser unit tests
