## Goal (user story)

As the proxy maintainer, I want the unused `github` model chain (and its
`github-primary` provider entry) removed from `proxy/config.yaml`, so the
configuration reflects reality and carries no dead routing surface that could
silently attract traffic or confuse future readers.

## Evidence that it is unused

- `proxy/config.yaml` lines ~346-352 declare a `models.github` chain with a
  single remote provider `github-primary` (endpoint
  `https://models.inference.ai.azure.com`, aliases `github-*`).
- Zero traffic in every available proxy log (2026-10-17 14:46 → 2026-10-24
  10:35): no `provider=GitHub`, no `entry=github`, no `github-primary`, no
  `models.inference.ai` occurrences.
- In the 24h usage window (2026-10-23 10:52 → 2026-10-24 10:52) only three
  initial providers appear across 175 sessions: OpenCode, MunitoAI, and
  local/Qwen3.
- No test in tests/ or proxy/tests/ references the github chain.
- The only other reference is documentation: docs/routing.md:297 notes
  `github-primary` is deliberately ungated (no `model` declared). That note
  must be removed/updated with the chain.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: The `github` chain (provider entry `github-primary` and its
  `github-*` aliases) is removed from proxy/config.yaml; no other chain
  references it.
- AC2: The resulting config loads cleanly — proxy startup/config-load tests
  pass, and a config validation/merge test confirms no dangling alias or
  provider reference remains.
- AC3: Documentation is consistent: docs/routing.md no longer describes
  `github-primary` as an ungated provider (remove the paragraph or restate it
  for a surviving ungated entry), and any config header comment naming it is
  updated.
- AC4: A regression test asserts the `github` chain is absent (config-load
  test), so the dead entry cannot be reintroduced unnoticed.
- AC5: If any client is found to request a `github-*` model alias (grep of
  shipped client configs), that must be reported and resolved before removal
  — otherwise AC1/AC4 stand.
- AC6: Full suite passes via the test skill before the change is closed.

## Notes

- The upstream model is unreachable anyway: `github-primary` declares no
  `model`, so the client chooses it; nothing in this deployment exercises
  that path. Removal also drops the "deliberately NOT gated" special case in

  `author`, `code`, `compact`.

## Goal (user story)

As a maintainer and analyst, I want a single per-turn correlation identifier
carried on every structured log line, so a request's full lifecycle — local
routing decision, fallbacks, stream start, stream finish, tokens — can be
reconstructed exactly instead of by FIFO pairing and nearest-line heuristics.

## Why

Today a turn leaves a trail of lines tied together only by session UUID and
timestamp ordering: `routing_skip_local` -> `Fallback triggered` xN ->
`Stream started` -> `Stream finished`. The analysis skill compensates with
heuristics (FIFO stream pairing, 60s fallback windows, nearest-attribution)
that mis-assign reasons (see the rate_limited misattribution in the
2026-10-23/24 window, where a session's own lease denials were overwritten by
an unrelated session's fallback line). A per-request id would remove every
one of these heuristics.

## Design note (plan in implementation)

Emitting an id at the earliest point a request is known (accept/entry) and
carrying it on: `routing_skip_local`, `routing_skip_provider_context`,
`Fallback triggered`, `routing_hop`, `local_dispatch_denied`, `[local]/[remote]
POST`, `Stream started`, `Stream finished`, `dispatch_first_byte_ms=`,
`ttft_seconds=`, and the error lines. Short (e.g. 8-hex) to keep lines
readable; both local and remote paths are in different modules
(`proxy/provider.py`, `proxy/router.py`, `proxy/proxy_remote.py`), so this is
a cross-cutting change with a shared helper.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: A shared helper (e.g. in `proxy/utils.py` or a new module) generates
  and stamps a per-turn id, and the id is carried on all structured line
  kinds listed above (verify each emit site; no line kind may be left with
  the id unconditionally absent).
- AC2: The id is stable across the full lifecycle of one client request —
  including across fallback hops and chain-hold re-emissions — and unique per
  turn of a session (at minimum within the session).
- AC3: The usage-analysis skill consumes the id:
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/log_parser.py` parses it onto the
  relevant events; `aggregation.py` pairs streams, fallbacks, skips and TTFT
  events by id (falling back to today's heuristics only when the id is
  absent in older logs); `reporting.py` documents that per-turn attribution is
  exact where ids exist.
- AC4: Skill tests: `tests/fixtures.py` lines with ids; new tests prove
  exact pairing by id (fallback -> stream, skip -> stream, TTFT -> stream)
  and that legacy lines without ids still parse via the existing fallback
  paths.
- AC5: Proxy tests asserting log text are updated where they instantiate or
  assert these lines: `proxy/tests/test_provider_fallback.py`,
  `proxy/tests/test_model_audit_plan_routing.py`,
  `proxy/tests/test_contention_queue_profile.py`.
- AC6: Other log consumers audited/updated: `scripts/idle_admit_impact.py`,
  `scripts/slot-persistence-correlate.py`,
  `scripts/analyse_slot_ratio_restore.py`,
  `scripts/prefill_recovery_verification.py`,
  `proxy/scripts/correlate_oversized_sessions.py`,
  `.worklog/analysis/extract_metrics.py`; the pass-through log tail in
  `proxy/proxy/ui.py` is verified unaffected.
- AC7: Documentation: `REFERENCE.md` documents the id field and the
  exact-attribution semantics; SKILL.md notes no behavioural change.
- AC8: Full suite passes via the test skill; no regression in the deterministic
  daily report path.

## Notes

- This supersedes most of the pairing heuristics in
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis`; the change is cross-cutting, so split
  into sub-tasks during planning (shared helper + emit sites; parsers; skill
  consumption; tests) if useful.
- Backwards compatibility mandatory: old logs without ids must keep parsing.
data.title: Add per-turn correlation id to all structured log lines

## Goal (user story)

As the proxy-usage analyst, I want `Stream finished` lines to say explicitly
when an upstream reported no token usage, so "no data" is distinguishable from
"zero tokens" and sessions with unknown context are countable rather than
invisible.

## Why

`proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` only appends `tokens=prompt/completion/total`
when the upstream response carries a `usage` object:

```
if isinstance(usage, dict): ... parts.append(f"tokens=...")
```

When a provider (or an aborted/errored stream) omits usage, the line silently
has no `tokens=` field. In the 2026-10-23/24 window this left 3 of the 26
local-using sessions with no context size at all (their `Stream finished`
lines carry no tokens), so any analysis of "context at fallback" for them
degrades to n/a with no way to tell why at the log level.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: When a terminal stream has no reportable usage, the `Stream finished`
  line carries an explicit marker (e.g. `tokens=missing` or `usage=none`),
  emitted from the same code path in `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`.
- AC2: The marker never overrides real usage — a present `usage` object still
  logs `tokens=p/c/t` exactly as today (no format change for the populated
  case).
- AC3: The usage-analysis skill counts the new marker:
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/log_parser.py` parses it onto the
  stream-finished event, and `aggregation.py`/`reporting.py` report a
  "streams without usage" count (window-level, and per-session where the
  context-at-fallback table is rendered) instead of silently emitting n/a.
- AC4: `reporting.py` limitation text in the affected sections names the
  marker as the cause of missing context figures.
- AC5: Tests: a fixture line with `tokens=missing` in
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/fixtures.py`, plus tests in
  `test_analyze_proxy_usage.py` proving (a) missing-usage streams are counted
  and excluded from token totals, and (b) populated lines are unchanged.
  Proxy-side test for the emit path in `proxy/tests/` (whichever suite covers
  `router_helpers` stream-finish logging).
- AC6: Other log consumers audited/updated: `scripts/idle_admit_impact.py`,
  `scripts/slot-persistence-correlate.py`,
  `proxy/scripts/analyze_context_distribution.py`,
  `.worklog/analysis/extract_metrics.py` (any code doing
  `tokens=` regex matches must not treat `missing` as a number).
- AC7: `REFERENCE.md` documents the marker and its meaning.
- AC8: Full suite passes via the test skill.

## Notes

- Small, contained change; the risk is consumers that regex
  `tokens=(\d+)/(\d+)/(\d+)` — those simply won't match the marker, which is
  the desired behaviour, but each should be verified rather than assumed.
data.title: Emit explicit tokens=missing marker when upstream reports no usage

## Goal (user story)

As a maintainer, I want the proxy's own request-budget skip to use a name that
cannot be confused with an upstream rate-limit rejection, so operators and
analysis tooling stop misreading `rate_limited` as "the local model was rate
limited".

## Why

`rate_limited` is emitted by `proxy/proxy/provider_budget.py` when a provider
entry's configured `rate_limit_rpm` window is exhausted
(`BudgetDecision(reason="rate_limited")`). It is a **proxy-side, pre-flight
budget skip**, not an HTTP 429 from the provider — upstream 429s are logged
separately as `[remote] upstream error status=429` /
`upstream_http_error`.

The name caused a concrete misreading: `rate_limited` is 61.6% of the
fallback-reason table (6,042 events, all `from=munitoai-free`), yet it was
reported as the per-session "reason for remote fallback" for 11 of 26
sessions that had actually been diverted from local by lease contention. The
local provider has no `rate_limit_rpm` and can never emit this reason (0 of
9,683 archive occurrences are `from=local`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: The budget-skip reason is emitted as `provider_budget_exhausted`
  (retaining the `_after_wait` / `_waiters` / `_disconnect` variants, e.g.
  `provider_budget_exhausted_after_wait`), from
  `proxy/proxy/provider_budget.py` and the `fallback_reason = ...` assignments
  in `proxy/proxy/provider.py`.
- AC2: Internal status/behaviour is unchanged: `_BUDGET_SKIP_STATUSES`, the
  affinity/reserve/wait logic, and any cooldown behaviour keep working (the
  rename must not alter decisions). Update any internal constant that keys on
  the old string.
- AC3: The usage-analysis skill normalises legacy logs: `log_parser.py` maps
  `rate_limited*` -> `provider_budget_exhausted*` so historical windows and
  new windows report under one label, with the mapping documented in
  `REFERENCE.md` (add to the existing legacy reason mapping next to
  `warm_cache_bypass` -> `context_too_large`).
- AC4: `reporting.py` renders the new label and keeps the reason table stable
  (no duplicate rows for old/new names in one window);
  `recommendations.py` text that references rate limiting is updated to
  distinguish proxy budget pacing from upstream 429s.
- AC5: Tests: parser normalisation tests (old and new spellings) in
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/`; proxy tests that assert the reason
  string are updated (`proxy/tests/test_provider_fallback.py`,
  `proxy/tests/test_contention_queue_profile.py`,
  `proxy/tests/test_local_admission_guard.py`,
  `proxy/tests/test_model_audit_plan_routing.py`).
- AC6: Other log consumers audited/updated:
  `scripts/idle_admit_impact.py`, `scripts/slot-persistence-correlate.py`,
  `proxy/benchmarks/munitoai_budget_eval.py`,
  `proxy/benchmarks/contention_queue_profile.py`,
  `.worklog/analysis/extract_metrics.py`.
- AC7: `REFERENCE.md` documents the vocabulary split (proxy budget skip vs
  upstream HTTP 429) so the two are never conflated again.
- AC8: Full suite passes via the test skill.

## Notes

- Deliberately deferred behind the session-attribution fixes: renaming alone
  does not fix mis-attribution, it only removes a misleading label. Land the
  session field on `Fallback triggered` first so the report is correct
  regardless of naming.
- Coordinate: dashboards/UI that display reason strings (the log tail in
  `proxy/proxy/ui.py` shows raw lines) need only a display sanity check.
data.title: Rename budget-skip reason rate_limited to provider_budget_exhausted

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want local prompt-eval (prefill) throughput increased so that
large cold prompts become cheap enough to serve locally, unlocking real local
utilisation instead of diverting work to paid remote providers.

## GATING PRECONDITION — do not start before this is met

**This item must only be executed once we have had a successful night of local
LLM consumption, meaning >60% GPU utilisation across a full night.** Until
local actually carries sustained work (>60% local busy), tuning prefill
throughput is premature: there is no sustained workload to measure against and
no evidence that prefill latency — rather than routing policy — is the binding
constraint. Verify the gate with the `proxy-usage-analysis` report's
`## Local model utilization` section for a night window (e.g. 22:00-07:00):
it must show busy >= 60%. Record that evidence in a comment on this item
before starting work; if the gate is not met, leave the item blocked.

## Why (current evidence, for context once the gate is met)

- Prompt-eval speed (llama-server eval timing, Qwen3, fast bucket): median
  **90.7 tok/s**, p90 316.7, p10 24.9 (532 samples, 24h window
  2026-10-23 10:52 -> 2026-10-24 10:52).
- Per-stream prefill (dispatch -> first byte): p50 4.4s, p90 35.3s, max 73.7s.
- `local_prefill_deadline_seconds: 90` — a slow prefill can be cancelled, and
  prior incidents show cancelled prefills re-dispatching identical prompts
  (the prefill-thrash cooldown exists because of this).
- The prefill-ETA admission guard refused **478** local admissions in the
  window on projected prefill cost, and only **34** requests were admitted by
  the idle override despite local being idle 89.8% of the time.
- Current llama-server launch flags (Qwen3 child):
  `--ctx-size 262144 --parallel 2 --batch-size 8192 --ubatch-size 1024
  --cache-ram 40960 --cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v q8_0
  --swa-checkpoints 32 --no-mmap -ngl 80 --threads 8`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC0 (GATE): A comment on this item records the measured >60% GPU utilisation
  for a full night, taken from the usage-analysis report, before any change is
  made. Work does not start without it.
- AC1: A measured baseline is captured first: prompt-eval tok/s distribution
  (p10/p50/p90), prefill phase duration, prefill-ETA admission refusals, and
  prefill-thrash events over a fixed window, all from the
  `proxy-usage-analysis` artifacts.
- AC2: Prefill throughput is improved by tuning the llama-server launch
  configuration (candidates: `--ubatch-size` 1024 -> 2048/4096, `--batch-size`,
  `--mlock`, thread count, SWA/checkpoint settings) and/or the prefill-related
  proxy knobs (`local_prefill_deadline_seconds`, the ETA guard budget). Each
  changed value is justified by measurement, not by guesswork.
- AC3: The optimisation is measured with the same method as AC1 and the
  before/after comparison is recorded on this item, including any effect on
  decode speed (no regression to decode tok/s median) and on stability
  (`slot_save failed`, prefill cancellations, HTTP 400/503 rates).
- AC4: If a knob change affects the prefill-ETA guard's behaviour, the guard's
  configuration and documentation are updated together, and the
  `local_prefill_deadline_seconds` / ETA interactions are documented.
- AC5: The usage-analysis skill is updated if new or changed log evidence is
  needed to measure the improvement
  (`.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/{llama_log_parser.py,log_parser.py,
  reporting.py}`, `REFERENCE.md`), and any other log-consuming script that
  reads llama-server eval timings or prefill evidence is audited
  (`proxy/scripts/replay_prefill_occupancy.py`,
  `scripts/prefill_recovery_verification.py`,
  `scripts/prefill_lease_verification.py`).
- AC6: Launch-flag changes are documented in `models.ini` / start-proxy
  documentation so the settings are reproducible, and any start-proxy script
  or test asserting the flags is updated.
- AC7: Full suite passes via the test skill.

## Notes

- This item is downstream of routing policy: raising local demand (thresholds,
  serve-first admission) comes first, otherwise there is nothing to optimise
  for. Keep the gate.
- Related: LP-0MSAOQTJS000FFVM (evaluate increasing local ctx-size) and the
  slot-geometry experiment (1 slot vs 2) — decide ctx/slot geometry before
  micro-tuning batch sizes, since the two interact.
data.title: Optimise llama-server prefill latency to unlock local utilisation

data.description:
## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want a measured comparison of **1 llama-server slot with
262,144 ctx** versus **2 slots with 131,072 ctx each**, so we can choose the
geometry that maximises local work served without unacceptable queueing.

## GATING PRECONDITION — do not start before this is met

**This experiment can only be carried out when we have a full night of GPU use
(>60% busy).** With local currently at ~10% busy, a 1-vs-2 slot comparison
measures noise, not saturation: the trade-off only shows up when demand
actually contends for slots. Verify the gate with the
`proxy-usage-analysis` report's `## Local model utilization` section for a
complete night window: busy must be >= 60% for the full night. Record that
evidence in a comment on this item before starting; if the gate is not met,
leave the item blocked.

## Why (current evidence, for context once the gate is met)

- Current geometry: `--parallel 2` with `--ctx-size 262144` = **131,072 tokens
  per slot**.
- Measured concurrency: **avg 1.04 while busy, peak 2** — demand is nearly
  serial today, so 2 slots are rarely both used.
- The routing hard cap (`local_large_context_warm_cache_threshold: 120000`)
  sits just under the 131K per-slot limit. In the 24h window **2,064 requests
  were skipped as `context_too_large`** (estimated > 120K), including 105
  skips from sessions that were already warm (cache ratio 0.92-1.00, only ~4K
  new tokens, total 126K-137K). A single 262K slot would move that ceiling
  from ~120K to ~258K.
- Local was idle **89.8%** of the window, serving only 225 turns across 26
  sessions, so spare capacity is not the current constraint — but slot
  geometry determines what will be servable once demand is raised.

## Hypothesis to test

- **1 x 262K**: ~2x per-slot context → far fewer `context_too_large` skips and
  larger conversations stay local; cost: requests serialise when two sessions
  overlap (today: peak 2, avg 1.04, so the cost may be small).
- **2 x 131K**: current state; parallel but capped at ~120K per request; the
  evidence above shows warm sessions being cut off at the cap.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC0 (GATE): A comment records the measured >60% GPU busy for a full night
  from the usage-analysis report, before any configuration change.
- AC1: A repeatable measurement protocol is defined and written on this item:
  identical workload window length, same metrics, same report tooling for both
  arms.
- AC2: Arm A (2 x 131K, current) and Arm B (1 x 262K) are each run for a
  comparable period at the gate, with llama-server `--parallel` / `--ctx-size`
  changed together (and `session_slot_pool_size` plus the warm/cold thresholds
  adjusted consistently, since per-slot ctx and slot count interact — see
  LP-0MSAZXXDY005AWA1 / LP-0MSI2M5BT004BCDP on the band collapsing to zero
  width).
- AC3: Results compare, for each arm: local busy %, turns served locally,
  requests diverted per fallback reason (especially `context_too_large` and
  `large_context_bypass`), queue wait / `fallback_after_queue` counts, time to
  first token, prefill and decode phase slot-seconds, and any errors
  (`slot_save failed`, HTTP 400/503).
- AC4: A decision is recorded on this item: keep 2 slots, move to 1 slot, or
  make it mode-dependent, with the data that justifies it. If 1 slot wins, the
  follow-on config change is filed (or implemented if in scope).
- AC5: Findings feed the configuration documentation (`models.ini` launch
  flags, `proxy/config.yaml` slot/ctx comments) and the usage-analysis skill's
  interpretation section if the guidance changes
  (`.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/REFERENCE.md`), plus any log-consuming
  script that assumes a fixed slot count or per-slot ctx.
- AC6: Full suite passes via the test skill for any config/code change made.

## Notes

- Depends on demand having been raised first (thresholds / serve-first
  admission); that is why the >60% busy gate exists.
- Related: LP-0MSAOQTJS000FFVM (local ctx-size evaluation), and the
  prefill-latency optimisation item — decide geometry before micro-tuning.
data.title: Experiment: 1 slot at 262K ctx vs 2 slots at 131K ctx

data.description:
## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want the proxy to record real prompt/completion token usage
for local streams, so that (a) local cache-credit and context accounting can
work from measured data and (b) the usage-analysis report can measure actual
local prompt sizes instead of showing them as unknown.

## Why (evidence)

Local `Stream finished` lines **never carry `tokens=`**:

- 225 of 225 local `Stream finished` lines in the window 2026-10-23 10:52 ->
  2026-10-24 10:52 have no token field;
- **0** lines with `tokens=` exist in the entire log archive (2026-10-17 ->
  2026-10-24) for `provider=local`.

Consequences:

1. **The usage-based cache-credit path is dead for local.** In
   `proxy/router.py` (~line 566) `update_cached_ratio()` and
   `record_prompt_prefix()` are only called when the response carries a usage
   block with `prompt_tokens > 0`. Because local never reports usage, the
   expected-reuse credit (`LP-0MVI2XOTY008Q4UV`) can never be earned from
   measured tokens. Credit today comes only from the slot-snapshot seeding
   path (655 `slot_save success` events in the archive), so a session whose
   first local dispatch did not produce a snapshot stays permanently "cold"
   (ratio 0.00) and is then bypassed by the 38K cold-cache rule on every later
   turn.
2. **The report cannot measure local context.** In the window, 3 of the 26
   sessions that used local had no context size at all, and the per-model
   token table attributes local tokens only via sessions whose *initial*
   provider was local — not via actual local streams.
3. Two current analysis outputs are therefore guesses rather than
   measurements: per-session local prompt sizes, and the cache-state
   attribution used in the skip-reason explanation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: Local `Stream finished` lines include `tokens=prompt/completion/total`
  with values taken from llama-server's reported usage (its response/`usage`
  payload or `/slots` accounting — whichever is authoritative), for
  non-streaming and streaming paths.
- AC2: `update_cached_ratio()` and `record_prompt_prefix()` therefore fire for
  local streams with measured values, so the expected-reuse credit is earned
  from data rather than only from a saved slot snapshot. Verify with a test
  that a 30K local turn followed by a 40K total / 10K new turn routes local
  (the intended cold-cap semantics: the cap applies to NEW, uncached tokens).
- AC3: A regression test proves the sequential-caching case explicitly:
  turn 1 total 30K -> local; turn 2 total 40K with ~10K new -> still local
  (new tokens below the 38K cold cap). This is the behaviour the design
  intends and it currently cannot be demonstrated from the logs.
- AC4: The usage-analysis skill consumes the new data:
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/log_parser.py` and
  `aggregation.py` attribute tokens to local streams, `reporting.py` reports
  real local prompt sizes and a "streams without usage" count, and the
  limitation text that currently explains missing local context is updated.
- AC5: Other log consumers relying on `tokens=` are audited:
  `scripts/idle_admit_impact.py`, `scripts/slot-persistence-correlate.py`,
  `proxy/scripts/analyze_context_distribution.py`,
  `.worklog/analysis/extract_metrics.py`.
- AC6: Tests: skill fixtures/tests in
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/` plus proxy-side tests for the emit
  path.
- AC7: `REFERENCE.md` documents local token reporting and the cold-cap
  semantics (cap applies to new/uncached tokens; total context is bounded
  separately by the warm cap).
- AC8: Full suite passes via the test skill.

## Notes

- Complements LP-0MVMBM6N400541EH (`tokens=missing` marker): that item makes
  absence explicit; this item fixes the root cause (local usage is never
  reported at all, so the marker would fire on every local stream).
- Do not change routing thresholds here — this is measurement plumbing, and it
  is a prerequisite for measuring any later routing change honestly.
data.title: Report real token usage for local streams (cold-cap/unlock + measurable context)

data.description:
## Problem statement

Local admission is scheduled **per request** against a 2-slot llama-server pool
with no session→slot tenancy and no check of the *actual* reusable prefix, so
any session can land on another session's slot and lose the resident KV. 27
distinct sessions cycled through 2 slots in ~5.4 h on 2026-10-24; aggregate
prefix reuse was 26.1 % and the median for prompts >20k tokens was **15.6 %**
(28 of 227 fully cold), and 160 `prefill_deadline_exceeded` cancellations in
5.4 h wasted ~780k prefill tokens (~93 % of local compute in the window).

The routing estimator cannot see this: `cached_ratio` is predicted from the
session's own snapshot sidecar (`proxy/proxy/slot_cache_ratio.py`) and is
structurally wrong under contention (`cached_ratio ≈ 0.99` predicted for
requests that then prefilled from `n_past=738`), which is why the 38k cold cap
never fired. The counter-example that proves it is slot churn rather than
GPU incapacity: the identical 49,103-token prompt scored `n_past=738` on its
first attempt (deadline-cancelled) and **100 % reuse (`n_past=49103`)** on the
immediate same-prompt retry, before another session trashed the slot.

## Users

- **Primary — local-work sessions (herdr / opencode clients):** multi-turn
  coding sessions with large, mostly-resident context that today lose their
  prefix on nearly every turn.
- **Secondary — the proxy operator:** needs local throughput without paying
  remote tokens for work the GPU could have done, and needs a truthful signal
  when local admission declines.
- **Tertiary — the capacity/usage analyst:** consumes the usage report to
  attribute local vs remote dispatch and resident-vs-evicted reuse.

User stories:

- *As a multi-turn local session*, my second and later turns should resume
  from my resident prefix instead of a cold prefill that consumes my whole
  deadline.
- *As the proxy operator*, a cold prompt that cannot finish inside the prefill
  deadline must not be admitted just because a prediction said it would be
  cheap.
- *As the operator*, I want to see, per admission decision, the measured
  reusable prefix and which session owned the slot, so residency regressions
  are visible without forensics.
- *As a client whose connection died*, I must not leave a dead session holding
  the pool; the proxy alone reaps me within a bounded window.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Resident-prefix admission gate.** Before a local dispatch of a large prompt is admitted, the router computes the session's *actual* reusable prefix from live slot state and admits only when `reuse_ratio = min(context_tokens, estimated_tokens) / estimated_tokens` is `>= local_resident_prefix_min_ratio` (default `0.5`, `0` disables). Otherwise it skips local with reason `resident_prefix_insufficient` and the chain falls through as it does today. Cold prompts above the admission budget from non-resident sessions are never admitted. *Measured by:* unit tests over stubbed slot snapshots + a replay fixture of the 2026-10-24 window asserting zero over-budget cold admissions.
- **AC2 — Session tenancy ("N tenants, 2 slots").** At most `local_session_tenants` distinct sessions (default: the slot count, i.e. 2) may hold a local reservation for a large prompt at once. A new session's large prompt is admitted only when a slot is free of other sessions' prefixes, or when the resident session's tenancy has idle-lapsed (`local_session_tenancy_idle_seconds`, default derived from the existing adaptive dispatch lease). Beyond that bound the request follows the normal chain rather than evicting a resident session.
- **AC3 — Live-prefix pricing (re-scoped).** The cold-cache gate (`provider._should_skip_local`) prices `new_tokens` from the **live** measurement used by AC1 rather than the predicted sidecar ratio, so the new-token cap is evaluated against real prefill work. The budget constant itself is owned by `LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D` (25k) and is consumed, not redefined, here. *Measured by:* zero admissions whose live `new_tokens > cold threshold` unless idle-exempt.
- **AC4 — Deadline/thrash regression (re-anchored), verified by a mandatory follow-up work item.** On a 24 h window measured **after** `LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D` is deployed, scheduling-attributed `prefill_deadline_exceeded` events are >= 90 % below that window's own re-anchored baseline; genuine GPU-speed misses are out of scope. ## Constraints

- **`/slots` must not be queried on the admission hot path.** Under a
  prompt-processing batch llama-server holds `/slots` for >15 s (measured 8.7 s
  then >15 s, vs the 1 s status timeout) — see `LP-0MUXTW4MD003TVIC`. AC1 must
  therefore read the in-memory snapshot already maintained every ~1 s by
  `_periodic_broadcast_loop()` (`observability._last_slot_details_cache`,
  TTL-coalesced `/slots` poll, 5 s failure backoff) plus
  `session._slot_owners`; any synchronous upstream call is prohibited.
- **Fail-open on unknown state.** A missing/stale snapshot, an unreported
  `context_tokens` (llama b8782 dropped `n_past`), or a cache older than the
  freshness bound must not turn into a hard local outage: fall back to the
  session-owns-slot check, then to today's predicted-ratio decision.
- **No change to** `local_prefill_deadline_seconds` (stays a backstop;
  `LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D` owns the 90→110 change) and no change to
  `local_max_concurrent_prefills`.
- **No live slot-count change** here: widening the snapshot pool is evaluated
  separately in `LP-0MVN3KPEC007WWL5`, and adding llama slots shrinks per-slot
  context (262,144 → 87,381 at 3 slots), excluding the long-context sessions
  that dominate this workload.
- **Idle-awareness must keep working.** `local_idle_admit_enabled`
  (`LP-0MVGD9Z8Z0055Y5J`) deliberately overrides the economic bypass when the
  GPU is idle; the new gate must not silently disable that behaviour.
- `contention_queue_*` semantics are unchanged: a request denied by AC1/AC2
  does not consume the queue budget differently from today's bypass path.

## Existing state

- Admission is per-request: `router_helpers._try_acquire_local_dispatch()`
  keeps N concurrent dispatch leases (`local_active_queries`,
  `local_dispatch_records`, no-preemption cooldown), which bounds *in-flight*
  requests but not *which* sessions occupy the pool over time.
- The economic gate is `provider._should_skip_local()`: a hard
  `warm_cache_threshold` cap plus `new_tokens = estimated_tokens *
  (1 - cached_ratio)` compared to the cold threshold, where `cached_ratio`
  comes from `_last_cached_ratio` and the snapshot sidecar
  (`slot_cache_ratio.py`, safety margin 0.9, prefix-fingerprint validated).
- Slot ownership/persistence already exists: `session._slot_owners`
  (`(endpoint, slot_id) -> session_id`), `_slot_id_for_session`,
  `_free_slot_assignment`, `_save_slot_snapshot` / `_restore_slot_snapshot`
  with per-slot failure cooldowns and `session_slot_skip_when_busy: true`.
- Live slot state is already collected: `observability._query_slots_detail()`
  (single-flight, 1 s TTL, 5 s failure backoff) feeds
  `_last_slot_details_cache`; log-derived progress (`_slot_progress_cache`,
  60 s max age) supplements builds that dropped `n_past`.
- Mitigations already shipped: post-deadline thrash cooldown
  (`LP-0MVKUKFHH005UDWL`, 10 min default), no-progress watchdog + prefill
  liveness extension (`LP-0MUCEFB8E003YVFF`, `LP-0MVKUKFSO008GI6O`),
  atomic reservations (`admission_reserve.py`).
- Measured gap: none of the above consults the *live* resident prefix, and
  none bounds the number of distinct sessions contending for the pool.

## Desired change

1. **Residency view (shared, in-memory).** Build a small read-only projection
   of `(slot_id, owner_session, context_tokens, is_processing, age)` from
   `_last_slot_details_cache` + `session._slot_owners`, exposed as one function
   used by AC1, AC2, AC3 and AC5. No new poller, no upstream call, no lock
   inversion (read under a snapshot copy).
2. **Admission ladder** in `_should_skip_local` / the local dispatch path:
   (i) hard `warm_cache_threshold` cap (unchanged); (ii) **resident-prefix
   gate** (AC1) with the fallback ladder — `context_tokens` known → measured
   ratio; unknown but session owns the slot → treat as resident (restore
   path); otherwise → non-resident; (iii) **tenancy** check (AC2); (iv) cold
   pricing from live `new_tokens` (AC3); (v) existing idle-exempt override
   stays last, so an idle GPU still serves cold work.
3. **Tenancy as a lease** registered alongside the existing dispatch records
   (AC6), reaped by `_dispatch_cleanup_loop` and the no-progress watchdog, so
   no new lifecycle machinery is introduced.
4. **Logging + report** (AC5) using the existing structured log lines rather
   than a new sink.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk: admission starvation.** A strict residency gate could refuse local
  for most large prompts, shifting cost to remote. *Mitigation:* the idle-exempt
  override stays last in the ladder, the gate is configurable (0 disables),
  and AC5 logging makes the shift visible within one report cycle.
- **Risk: stale snapshot decisions.** A 1 s TTL snapshot can be wrong exactly
  at a slot switch. *Mitigation:* reason about ownership (authoritative
  in-process registry) rather than throughput, and fail-open on unknown state.
- **Risk: `/slots` unobservability repeats** (`LP-0MUXTW4MD003TVIC`), leaving
  `context_tokens` unknown. *Mitigation:* the fallback ladder + log-derived
  progress cache; the feature must remain correct when the number is absent.
- **Risk: tenancy + single-flight interaction** can make a session wait behind
  its own earlier turn; *Mitigation:* same-session re-acquisition is always
  permitted (existing lease semantics), and the tenancy check only gates
  *new* sessions.
- **Risk: the 0.5 default is aggressive for this workload.** Measured median
  reuse is 15.6 % for prompts >20k, so a 0.5 default may refuse most large
  prompts initially. *Mitigation:* one knob, `0` disables, staged observation
  via AC5 logs before the AC4 window; the ladder still admits same-slot
  residents and idle-exempt work.
- **Assumption:** the local pool stays at 2 slots and
  `session_slot_pool_size: 2` for the duration of this work; a pool-size change
  (`LP-0MVN3KPEC007WWL5`) invalidates the tenancy default and the AC4 baseline.
- **Assumption:** `session._slot_owners` stays accurate under churn — verified
  by `LP-0MTIHWYGJ006YS6X` continuity tests; new tests extend them.
- **Assumption:** the 25k budget from `LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D` is the constant
  consumed by AC3; if that item changes scope, AC3's threshold follows it.
- **Scope-creep risk:** "more slots", snapshot-pool widening, and checkpoint
  tuning are adjacent opportunities — they stay linked work items
  (`LP-0MVN3KPEC007WWL5`), not additions to this brief.

data.description:
## Goal

Stop admitting local prefills that cannot possibly finish before the prefill deadline, and widen the deadline enough to admit the largest genuinely feasible prompt:

1. **Cold-prefill admission budget = 25,000 tokens** of *new* (uncached / to-be-prefilled) tokens — a cap on what the GPU must actually compute, not on prompt size.
2. **`local_prefill_deadline_seconds`: 90 → 120 s.** Operator decision: keep the 25k budget and widen the time budget rather than reducing the prompt budget. At the measured 20–30k band rate (249 t/s) a 25k prefill is ~100 s, i.e. ~16 % margin under 120 s (and ~93 s / ~23 % margin at the band's p75 rate of ~270 t/s).

## Why (measured on this host, 2026-10-24/25)

Prompt-eval rates from `llama-server` logs (268 samples), size-dependent with a knee at ~27k:

| Prompt | Median rate | Prefill |
|---|---|---|
| 10–20k | 281 t/s | 36–71 s |
| 20–30k | 249 t/s | 80–100 s |
| 30–40k | 181 t/s | 165–210 s |
| 48k | 152 t/s | ~320 s |
| 63k | 114 t/s | ~563 s |

Consequences measured in the 2026-10-24 18:38–23:47 window: **160 `prefill_deadline_exceeded` events**, 45 local tasks cancelled mid-prefill, **~780k of ~840k prefill tokens computed then discarded (~93 % waste)**. A 38k cold prefill (~210 s) can never fit a 90 s deadline; 25k (~100 s) fits 120 s with ~16 % margin.

## Concrete configuration proposal

All changes are in `proxy/config.yaml` (server section); nothing else changes.

| Key | Now | Proposed | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `local_prefill_deadline_seconds` | 90 | **120** | 25k cold ≈ 100 s at the measured 20–30k band rate (249 t/s): 90 s cancels it, 120 s admits it with ~16 % margin (~23 % at p75). Ordering stays `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds (60) < deadline (120) < local_dispatch_first_byte_timeout_seconds (840) < local_dispatch_max_prefill_seconds (900)` and below the client's 900 s queue deadline. |
| `local_cold_prefill_budget_tokens` *(new)* | — | **25000** (0 = disabled/rollback) | Hard cap on **new (to-be-prefilled) tokens** at admission, enforced on **every** admission path including `routing_idle_admit` (the economic bypass admitted 38 oversized requests in the window and is a direct leak). Refuse at admission with `reason=prefill_budget_exceeded`; never dispatch-then-cancel. |
| `local_admission_guard_eta_percentile_min_tokens` *(new; currently the hard-coded `CONSERVATIVE_MIN_TOKENS = 32_768` in `prefill_eta.py`)* | 32768 | **20000** | Extend the existing p75 ETA percentile pricing down to cover the 25k budget band. p75 ≈ 270 t/s for 20–30k → 25k ≈ 93 s ≤ 0.95 × 120 = 114 s ✓ admitted; 30–40k band p75 ≈ 190 t/s → 132 s ✗ refused. This is what stops a band-slow 25k from slipping past the flat cap. |
| `local_admission_guard_budget_safety_fraction` *(new)* | — | **0.95** | Admit only when `eta_prefill_p75 ≤ 0.95 × deadline` (= 114 s at 120 s). Makes the budget deadline-relative instead of a bare token count, so future deadline changes stay consistent. |
| `local_admission_guard_reference_tokens` | 32000 | **25000** | Align the published-status reference prompt with the budget (one number instead of two). |
| `local_prefill_thrash_cooldown_seconds` | 600 | **600 (unchanged)** | Now a backstop only; leave as-is. |
| `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds` / `contention_queue_max_depth` | 60 / 8 | unchanged | Budget refusal happens before the queue. |
| Slot count / `session_slot_pool_size` | 2 / 2 | unchanged | Out of scope (see LP-0MVN3KPEC007WWL5). |

Left deliberately untouched: `cold_threshold` is *derived* (38000, from `_effective_large_context_thresholds` over per-slot ctx) and becomes a non-binding upper bound once the 25k measured budget exists; `local_admission_guard_eta_percentile` stays at 75 (it is simply applied from 20k upwards now).

Expected effect from the measured rates:

- >25k cold prompts (the 49k–93k thrash set): refused at admission → **zero** deadline cancellations for them (baseline: 160 events / 5.4 h, ~780k wasted tokens).
- 25k cold: 93–100 s, admitted and completed under the 120 s deadline.
- Warm requests (cached_ratio ≥0.9, e.g. 47k prompt / 549 new tokens): unchanged — the budget never binds.
- Residual deadline events: only genuine GPU-speed misses near the cap, priced at ≤114 s (p75).

Accepted trade-off of the 120 s choice: a near-budget prompt that *is* admitted and then lost consumes up to 114 s before the detour (vs 90 s today), +27 % worst-case waste per failed attempt — acceptable because the budget removes the systematically-doomed attempts, which were the source of the 93 % waste.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 — Budget:** `local_cold_prefill_budget_tokens: 25000` caps the **new (prefilled) tokens** admitted for a local dispatch, on all admission paths (including idle/economic bypass). Over-budget requests are refused at admission (skip local, chain detours), never dispatched and never cancelled at the deadline.
- **AC2 — Deadline:** `local_prefill_deadline_seconds: 120`. Enforce and assert the ordering `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds (60) < deadline (120) < local_dispatch_first_byte_timeout_seconds (840) < local_dispatch_max_prefill_seconds (900)`, and keep the deadline strictly below the client's 900 s queue deadline (config-load assertion).
- **AC3 — Deadline-relative pricing:** budget admission uses p75 percentile ETA pricing from 20k tokens upwards (`local_admission_guard_eta_percentile_min_tokens: 20000`) and admits only when `eta_prefill ≤ 0.95 × deadline` (114 s), so 25k at the 20–30k band is admitted and 25k in the 30–40k band is refused.
- **AC4 — Regression evidence:** over a 24 h window post-deploy, scheduling-attributed `prefill_deadline_exceeded` events are ≤10 % of the 2026-10-24 baseline (160 per 5.4 h), the AC7 eviction counter is zero for within-budget prompts, wasted-prefill tokens correspondingly reduced, and no increase in client-visible 503s / retries.
- **AC5 — Warm path unchanged:** warm requests remain admissible when total prompt size exceeds 25k (assert e.g. 47k prompt / 549 new tokens stays local).
- **AC6 — Documentation + rollback:** config comments state units, interaction with `cold_threshold`/`warm_threshold` and the admission guard, and the rollback values (budget 0, deadline 90, percentile-min 32768, safety fraction off).
- **AC7 — Record post-acceptance eviction as an ERROR (defect signal, not noise):** any local dispatch that was **accepted** (admitted, dispatch record created) and then **evicted before producing a first byte** must be recorded at **ERROR** log level — never WARNING/INFO — with a structured, machine-parseable event carrying at least: `session`, `reason` (`prefill_deadline` | `no_progress_watchdog` | `idle_timeout` | `orphan_cleanup` | `lease_evicted` | `slot_assignment_freed`), `estimated_tokens`, `new_tokens`, `eta_prefill_s`, `elapsed_s`, `slot_id`, and the llama task id where known. This covers every release path an accepted dispatch can suffer, so eviction after acceptance is unambiguously an error condition rather than expected churn; refusals **before** acceptance stay at their current level (a budget/ETA refusal is normal operation, not an error). Ship with: (a) a dedicated monotonic counter and per-reason breakdown exposed in the `--json` summary and the `proxy-usage-analysis` report (`local_evictions_after_acceptance`), (b) an alerting threshold of >0 for evictions of within-budget prompts, and (c) a documented triage rule that any such ERROR is treated as a defect and filed as a `test-failure`-class work item — it is exactly the signal that the budget/pricing model is wrong for a prompt band.

## Tests

- Unit: budget boundary (24,999 admitted / 25,001 refused); warm bypass above 25k prompt size; deadline ordering assertion rejects a violating config; safety-fraction maths (114 s at 120 s); band-slow 25k refused via p75 pricing.
- Integration: fixture replay of the 2026-10-24 thrash window → zero admitted cold prompts >25k; every refused request detours with a logged reason.
- AC7 (eviction-after-acceptance is an ERROR): for **each** release path an accepted dispatch can take (`prefill_deadline`, `no_progress_watchdog`, `idle_timeout`, `orphan_cleanup`, `lease_evicted`, `slot_assignment_freed`), assert exactly one ERROR-level structured event is emitted with the required fields (session, reason, estimated_tokens, new_tokens, eta_prefill_s, elapsed_s, slot_id, llama task id where known), and assert none is emitted at WARNING/INFO. Assert the inverse too: a **pre-acceptance refusal** (budget / ETA / admission-guard) produces **no** ERROR (normal operation, no false alarms). Assert the counter increments once per eviction and that `local_evictions_after_acceptance` appears in the `--json` summary and in the `proxy-usage-analysis` report with its per-reason breakdown. Replay the 2026-10-24 thrash window as a regression fixture: with AC1/AC3 in force the counter must be 0 for within-budget prompts (any non-zero count fails the test, because it means the pricing model admitted a doomed dispatch).

## Relationships

- discovered-from: LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG (resident-prefix/tenancy admission). This item delivers the *budget* half of that item's AC3 ahead of the scheduler work and must ship independently; AC3 of LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG is to be re-scoped to the live-prefix pricing half when this lands.
- Do not increase the number of live slots in this item (per-slot ctx shrinks 131k → 87.4k at 3 slots).

## Goal

Evaluate (with measurements, go/no-go) whether widening the **per-session KV snapshot pool** (`session_slot_pool_size` 2 → 4, snapshots under `session_slot_save_path/slot_<id>.bin`) raises local prefix reuse for the small/medium working set — as the recommended alternative to adding live llama slots, which would shrink per-slot context (262,144 → 87,381 at 3 slots) and exclude the long-context sessions that dominate this workload.

## Why

- Measured prefix reuse is poor: aggregate 26.1 %, median **15.6 %** for prompts >20k tokens (227 prompts), 28 fully cold; 27 distinct sessions cycled through a 2-slot pool in ~5.4 h.
- More live slots buy *residency*, not throughput (`local_max_concurrent_prefills: 1` serialises prefills), and cost per-slot address space for a long-context workload.
- The snapshot mechanism already exists (per-session save/restore, `session_slot_timeout_per_token_seconds: 0.0015`, capped at `session_slot_max_timeout_seconds: 60`, pool capped by `session_slot_pool_size: 2`) but is degraded under load (`session_slot_skip_when_busy: true`, circuit-breaker cooldown). Restore cost estimate: ~50k tokens ≈ 75 s → capped 60 s, so the mechanism currently helps only the <40k band.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 — Benchmark:** measure save/restore latency (and disk footprint) per prompt-size band (10k / 25k / 40k / 60k+) on the production GPU host, including under load (another session streaming), against the 0.0015 s/token timeout model.
- **AC2 — Go/no-go with evidence:** with `session_slot_pool_size: 4` in a replay/bake-off on the 2026-10-24 thrash window (or equivalent fixture), report the reuse uplift (baseline 15.6 % median for >20k prompts) and the restore-success rate (skip_when_busy / cooldown exclusions).
- **AC3 — If go:** ship the config change plus retention/eviction semantics for 4 snapshots (pool eviction policy, disk cap, failure cooldowns unchanged) and any report/observability fields (restore-hit rate per session, snapshot pool occupancy) so the proxy-usage-analysis report can monitor the effect.
- **AC4 — If no-go:** record the measured blockers (latency, skip rate, restore failures) as a comment on this item so the decision is reproducible.
- **AC5 — No change to live slot count or per-slot ctx in this item** (that remains the separate 3-slot "fast" profile discussion).

## Tests

Bake-off harness replaying fixture logs + real save/restore micro-benchmark on the host; unit tests for pool-size > 2 retention semantics; report-schema tests for the new fields.

## Relationships

- discovered-from: LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG (slot-churn / tenancy investigation, option 3a of the recommendation).
- This is an evaluation/deliberation item, not a mandate to change configuration.

## Goal

Execute the **24 h post-deploy verification of AC4** for
`LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG` (resident-prefix admission + session tenancy) and report
whether scheduling-attributed `prefill_deadline_exceeded` cancellations fell by
**>= 90 %** relative to that window's own re-anchored baseline.

**Earliest run: 2026-10-26T00:51Z.** That is the provable lower bound
(creation time + 24 h). The real instant is the **later** of
`LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG`'s deploy and `LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D`'s deploy, **+ 24 h** —
retitle this item with that concrete ISO-8601 UTC instant when both have
shipped. Do not run before it.

## Why

AC4 of `LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG` requires this verification, but it cannot be done
inside the implementation session: it needs a full 24 h production soak after
the scheduler change and after the cold-prefill budget change
(`LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D`, 25k tokens + deadline 90→110 s) are both deployed.
Keeping it here prevents the implementing session from measuring its own work
too early and calling it verified.

## Preconditions (check before running)

1. `LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG` is deployed to the proxy (resident-prefix gate, tenancy
   bound, live-prefix pricing, AC5 log fields present).
2. `LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D` is deployed (25k cold budget, 110 s deadline).
3. The proxy has been up continuously for the whole 24 h window — a restart
   inside the window invalidates the run (in-memory residency state resets).

## Measurement window

- 24 h, ending on a `05:00 UTC` boundary so it aligns with the daily
  `proxy-usage-analysis` cron report; record the exact start/end instants
  (ISO-8601 UTC) in the result comment.
- Re-anchor the baseline **to that same window** (post-budget-change), not the
  2026-10-24 figures (160 events / 5.4 h, ~780k wasted prefill tokens), which
  become historical reference only.

## Procedure

1. Base counts: `prefill_deadline_exceeded` events in the window, and total
   wasted prefill tokens.
2. Classify each event as *scheduling-attributed* when either
   (a) `reuse_ratio` logged at admission was below
   `local_resident_prefix_min_ratio`, or
   (b) `slot_owner_session` changed between admission and the deadline event
   (prefix evicted by another session).
   Everything else is a genuine GPU-speed miss and is out of scope.
3. Run the usage analysis for the window:
   `python3 .pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py`
   (see `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/SKILL.md` for options) and extract the
   resident-vs-evicted reuse split and slot-owner churn (AC5 signals).
4. Compare the scheduling-attributed residual against the re-anchored baseline
   and state the percentage reduction explicitly.

## Verdict criteria

- **PASS:** scheduling-attributed cancellations down **>= 90 %** vs the
  re-anchored baseline, with no `local_lease_active` refusal window exceeding
  the 180 s watchdog bound (AC6).
- **FAIL / follow-up:** either threshold missed → record the measured numbers,
  create a `discovered-from` item for the regression (with the offending log
  extract), and do not mark this item complete.

## Deliverable

A result comment on this item containing: window start/end, precondition
attestation (deploy times, proxy uptime), absolute event/token counts, the
scheduling-attributed split with the classifier applied, the percentage
reduction vs baseline, and the PASS/FAIL verdict. Then close with
`<WIP-id>: <summary>`.

## Links

- Verification target: `LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG` (AC4, AC5, AC6).
- Budget change whose deploy starts the clock: `LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D`.
- Historical baseline: `docs/dev/slot-thrashing-investigation/findings.md`,
  the 2026-10-24 18:38–23:47 proxy/llama-server logs under
  `/var/log/llama-proxy`.

As the implementing agent, I need an integration proof over the real 2026-10-24
thrash window that the new ladder refuses over-budget cold admissions and classifies
the resident retry correctly — so AC7's integration half and AC1's "replay fixture"
measurement are satisfied by evidence, not by unit stubs alone.

## Scope

Extend `proxy/scripts/replay_prefill_occupancy.py` (the existing replay driver for
admission verdicts) into the 2026-10-24 fixture driver: replay the pinned window,
recompute each request's verdict against the residency view reconstructed from the
log window, and assert (a) no cold admission above the budget without a resident
prefix and (b) the two named tasks classify as resident on the retry. The committed
fixture is a **reduced, sanitised extract** of the window (the raw 5.4 h log is not
committed); the script still supports pointing at the live log path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC7 (integration) — no over-budget cold admission:** replaying the pinned 2026-10-24 window through the new ladder asserts zero admissions whose live `new_tokens` exceeded the cold threshold without a resident prefix (idle-exempt admissions reported separately, not counted as violations).

data.description:
## Goal

Make post-acceptance eviction of a local dispatch an unambiguous **defect signal**: every release path that evicts an accepted dispatch *before its first byte* emits exactly one structured **ERROR** event with the full evidence set, and a dedicated monotonic counter tracks it (parent AC7, core half).

## Context

An accepted dispatch can be released before producing a first byte by six paths, and today each logs at a different level with no shared evidence:

| AC7 reason | Today's code path | Today's level |
|---|---|---|
| `prefill_deadline` | `router.py` `prefill_deadline_exceeded` + `router_helpers._release_prefill_deadline_dispatch` (`lease_released reason=prefill_deadline`) | WARNING / INFO |
| `no_progress_watchdog` | `router_helpers._cleanup_stale_local_dispatch` phase 1 (`reason=no_progress_watchdog`) | WARNING |
| `idle_timeout` | same function, inactive record past `expires_at` (`reason=idle_timeout`) | INFO |
| `orphan_cleanup` | same function, phase 3 (`reason=orphan_cleanup`) | WARNING + INFO |
| `lease_evicted` | `server._release_lease_on_session_eviction` → `lease_released reason=session_evicted` | INFO |
| `slot_assignment_freed` | `session._free_slot_assignment` (slot registry entry released) | no line of its own |

`lease_evicted` and `slot_assignment_freed` are AC7 vocabulary that does not exist yet; dispatch records today carry no `estimated_tokens`, `new_tokens`, `eta_prefill_s`, `slot_id` or first-byte flag, so the required evidence cannot be emitted without enriching the record at creation.

## Scope

**In:** dispatch-record enrichment, one shared emitter, ERROR-level structured event on all six paths, in-process counter + per-reason breakdown, `/admin/metrics` and Prometheus exposure, tests.

**Out:** the report/parser work (separate child), any change to *when* these paths fire (levels and evidence only), any change to the admission decision.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Post-acceptance eviction is an ERROR (parent AC7):** any local dispatch that was **accepted** (admitted, dispatch record created) and then **evicted before producing a first byte** must be recorded at **ERROR** log level — never WARNING/INFO — with a structured, machine-parseable event carrying at least: `session`, `reason` (`prefill_deadline` | `no_progress_watchdog` | `idle_timeout` | `orphan_cleanup` | `lease_evicted` | `slot_assignment_freed`), `estimated_tokens`, `new_tokens`, `eta_prefill_s`, `elapsed_s`, `slot_id`, and the llama task id where known. This covers every release path an accepted dispatch can suffer, so eviction after acceptance is unambiguously an error condition rather than expected churn; refusals **before** acceptance stay at their current level (a budget/ETA refusal is normal operation, not an error). One shared emitter produces the single line, e.g. `local_eviction_after_acceptance session=… reason=… estimated_tokens=… new_tokens=… eta_prefill_s=… elapsed_s=… slot_id=… llama_task_id=…`, emitted exactly once per eviction.
- **AC2 — Complete evidence.** The record is enriched at creation (in `router_helpers`, where the dispatch record is created) with `estimated_tokens`, `cached_ratio`, `new_tokens`, `eta_prefill_s` (the guard decision that admitted it, when known), `slot_id` and `llama_task_id` where known, plus an explicit `first_byte_seen` flag set when the first chunk arrives. Fields that are genuinely unknown are emitted as `unknown`/`0`, never omitted, so the line stays machine-parseable.
- **AC3 — Only accepted-and-unserved dispatches are errors.** `first_byte_seen == True` records are **not** eviction errors (a lease that expires after a served response is normal churn and stays at its current level). Records without a first-byte flag that are evicted for `idle_timeout` must be classified by the flag, not inferred from the path.
- **AC4 — Per-path tests.** For **each** of the six reasons, a test drives the release path and asserts exactly one ERROR-level `local_eviction_after_acceptance` event with all evidence fields, and asserts that no such event is emitted at WARNING/INFO. Inverse test: a pre-acceptance refusal (budget / ETA / admission guard) emits **no** event and does not increment the counter.
- **AC5 — Monotonic counter + per-reason breakdown.** `local_evictions_after_acceptance` increments exactly once per eviction, with a per-reason breakdown, reset only on process restart; exposed as a Prometheus counter (labelled by reason) and in the `/admin/metrics` JSON payload alongside the existing `guardrail_metrics` style blocks.
- **AC6 — Backwards-compatible logs.** Existing `lease_released … reason=…` lines keep their current names and levels (the report and other consumers parse them); the new structured ERROR line is additive, so a pre-change log parser still works.
- **AC7 — Triage-ready.** The event carries enough to file a `test-failure` item without log archaeology (reason + tokens + ETA + elapsed + slot), and the shipped config's budget/pricing admits it: a within-budget prompt must never produce this event (fixture replay: counter is 0).

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`
- `proxy/proxy/router.py`
- `proxy/proxy/server.py`
- `proxy/proxy/session.py`
- `proxy/proxy/metrics.py`
- `proxy/proxy/handlers.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_prefill_thrash_wedge.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_no_progress_watchdog.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_lease_truthfulness.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_slot_reuse_gap_analysis.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_local_eviction_after_acceptance.py` (new)

## Implementation sketch

1. Create the emitter (e.g. `proxy/proxy/local_eviction.py`) with `record_eviction_after_acceptance(srv=None, *, session, reason, record, extra)` → logs the ERROR line and increments the counter; idempotent per record (guard against double emit on a path that runs twice).
2. Enrich the dispatch record at creation and set `first_byte_seen` where the first chunk is observed.
3. Call the emitter from each of the six release paths, passing the record it already has; leave the existing log lines untouched.
4. Add the counter to `metrics.py` (`llama_local_evictions_after_acceptance_total{reason}`) and to `handlers.admin_metrics` JSON.
5. Write per-path tests + the inverse (refusal) test.

## Dependencies

- None (independent of the config/budget children). Must land before the usage-report child, which parses this event.

data.description:
## Goal

Surface post-acceptance evictions in the `proxy-usage-analysis` report and its `--json` summary, and record the alerting threshold plus the triage rule that turns each such event into a defect work item (parent AC7 reporting half, AC7(b), AC7(c)).

## Context

`summary_to_json` in `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/reporting.py` already exposes `local_admission_reject`, `local_admission_admit`, `local_idle_admit` and `errors_by_type`. The new ERROR event from the eviction child is not parsed yet, so the counter cannot be seen in the 24 h regression window (parent AC4) and the operator has no alert.

## Scope

**In:** log parser patterns, aggregation counters, `summary_to_json` keys, text report section, docs (alert threshold, triage rule).

**Out:** the proxy-side emitter (separate child), any change to existing report keys, alerting infrastructure outside the docs/report (no new Prometheus rule file unless one already exists to extend).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Parse.** `log_parser.py` recognises the `local_eviction_after_acceptance` ERROR line (all evidence fields, tolerant of missing `llama_task_id`/`slot_id`) and classifies it as its own event kind, never as a fallback/reason inheritance for neighbouring lines.
- **AC2 — Aggregate + JSON summary (parent AC7(a)).** `aggregation`/`reporting.summary_to_json` expose top-level `local_evictions_after_acceptance` (total) **and** a per-reason breakdown (e.g. `local_evictions_after_acceptance_by_reason`), with every one of the six reasons addressable (`prefill_deadline`, `no_progress_watchdog`, `idle_timeout`, `orphan_cleanup`, `lease_evicted`, `slot_assignment_freed`). Keys are additive: existing keys and their values are unchanged (regression test on a pre-change log fixture).
- **AC3 — Text report.** The human-readable report prints the counter and its per-reason breakdown, with the alert threshold (>0 for within-budget prompts) stated inline; `--quiet` still suppresses it.
- **AC4 — Alerting threshold documented (parent AC7(b)).** The skill's `SKILL.md`/report doc states the threshold: **any** `local_evictions_after_acceptance` for within-budget prompts is an alert, not a trend to watch.
- **AC5 — Triage rule documented (parent AC7(c)).** A documented rule (usage-analysis skill doc and the proxy runbook) that any such ERROR is treated as a defect and filed as a critical `test-failure`-class work item via the triage path, because it is exactly the signal that the budget/pricing model is wrong for a prompt band.
- **AC6 — Tests.** Parser test (full line, partial line, absence), aggregation test (per-reason counts), `summary_to_json` test (keys present, zero when absent), report-text test, and a pre-change-log regression test proving no existing key changed.

## Key Files

- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/log_parser.py`
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/aggregation.py`
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/reporting.py`
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/SKILL.md`
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py`
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_llama_log_parser.py`
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/recommendations.py`
- `proxy/docs/runbook-5xx.md`

## Implementation sketch

1. Add the regex + event kind + parser branch alongside the existing local-admission parsing.
2. Add `eviction_events` to the analysis result, with a `by_reason` counter.
3. Emit the two additive keys in `summary_to_json` and a report block next to the admission-guard block.
4. Document the threshold and triage rule where the other report thresholds live.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by "Post-acceptance eviction ERROR events and counter" (needs the event format).
data.title: Usage report eviction metrics and triage rule

data.description:
## Goal

Prove the shipped change with the parent's AC4 measurement: run the 24 h post-deploy window through `proxy-usage-analysis` and record the evidence (deadline-event rate vs the 2026-10-24 baseline, eviction counter for within-budget prompts, wasted-prefill tokens, client-visible 503/retry rate) on the parent item.

## Context

Parent AC4: scheduling-attributed `prefill_deadline_exceeded` events ≤10 % of the 2026-10-24 baseline (160 per 5.4 h ≈ 30/h), the AC7 eviction counter zero for within-budget prompts, wasted-prefill tokens correspondingly reduced, and no increase in client-visible 503s/retries. The window starts at the `POST /admin/reload-config`/restart that makes the new config live (per the intake note, a config reload is sufficient) — record that timestamp on this item before starting the measurement.

## Scope

**In:** post-deploy 24 h measurement, evidence recorded as a work-item comment, verdict + follow-up items.

**Out:** further code changes (any regression found becomes its own work item), the release/`dev`→`main` promotion.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Window defined and recorded.** The reload/restart timestamp that made the new config live is recorded before the window starts; the analysed window is ≥24 h after it.
- **AC2 — Regression evidence (parent AC4):** over the 24 h window post-deploy, scheduling-attributed `prefill_deadline_exceeded` events are ≤10 % of the 2026-10-24 baseline (160 per 5.4 h), the AC7 eviction counter is zero for within-budget prompts, wasted-prefill tokens correspondingly reduced, and no increase in client-visible 503s / retries. Each of the four checks is recorded with its measured number and pass/fail verdict; the ≤10 % check is the primary gate (≈3 events/h or fewer).
- **AC3 — Eviction counter (parent AC4/AC7).** `local_evictions_after_acceptance` is reported with its per-reason breakdown; pass requires **0** for within-budget prompts, and any non-zero count is recorded as a defect signal with a follow-up work item.
- **AC4 — Waste and client impact (parent AC4).** Wasted prefill tokens are compared with the ~780k baseline, and 503/retry counts are compared with the pre-change window; "no increase" is asserted with the actual numbers.
- **AC5 — Evidence + follow-ups.** Results are recorded as one structured comment on this item (numbers, window bounds, command used) and referenced from the parent; every failed check has a linked follow-up work item.
- **AC6 — Rollback decision.** If a check fails, the comment states which rollback knob(s) were applied (budget `0` / deadline `90` / percentile-min `32768` / safety fraction `0.0`) and why, or records an explicit decision to keep the change.

## Key Files

- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py`
- `proxy/config.yaml`
- `proxy/docs/routing.md`

## Implementation sketch

1. Note the reload timestamp; wait the full window (no early peeking that could bias the decision).
2. Run `analyze_proxy_usage.py --json` over the window plus the baseline window; capture both summaries.
3. Tabulate the four checks and record pass/fail with numbers.
4. File follow-ups for any failure; record the rollback decision.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by "Prefill budget/deadline config knobs + ordering assertion".
- Blocked by "Enforce cold-prefill budget on all admission paths".
- Blocked by "Post-acceptance eviction ERROR events and counter".
- Blocked by "Usage report eviction metrics and triage rule".
